picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. There's a monster Big 12 matchup on Halloween as Arizona heads to Texas Tech for a game between two 6-1 squads that will inevitably shake up the standings. My Arizona vs. Texas Tech prediction questions Will Hammond's quality, and the best of my college football picks takes a look at a total of 54.5 that might be too high. This game will be broadcast on ESPN at 12 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. TOP PICK Who will win Arizona vs Texas Tech: Arizona +3.5 Play Arizona at anything +3 or above. Texas Tech has a quarterback problem. Will Hammond has 13 turnover-worthy passes to pair with only eight big-time throws (per PFF), and his limitations have resulted in the third least-explosive passing attack in the nation . That makes them one-dimensional offensively, and it plays into Arizona's run-stopping defense. The Red Raiders don't block well enough up front (118th in front seven havoc allowed) to compensate for the quarterback deficiency. Tech's secondary has been hit for 266.1 passing yards per game, so the Wildcats (10th in passing success rate) will be able to chuck it around. Arizona vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 54.5 Tech's offensive limitations will show through in this matchup. Arizona's defense (14th in EPA per play, 11th in success rate) is much better than the market is accounting for, as it doesn't have name recognition but is well-coordinated under Danny Gonzales. On the flip side, Tech's defense checks in at 16th in EPA per play allowed and 10th in PFF's team defense grade. The strength of this team still resides on that side of the ball, and Joey McGuire will attempt to lean on that unit and minimize possessions for Fifita. Arizona's top three wide receivers have all been out. Tre Spivey is done for the year, while Giovanni Richardson and Chris Hunter III are considered questionable. The Wildcats can still move the ball in the air, but the efficiency won't be at its peak given the cluster injuries. Arizona vs Texas Tech combo Arizona got off to slow starts against Washington State and Northern Illinois, and could do so again during a difficult trip to Lubbock. Texas Tech has cashed the First Half Under in eight of its last 13 games. Given Hammond's turnover-prone ways and overall offensive issues, the defense should be the focal point over the second half of the season. Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. Arizona vs. Texas Tech Pick: Arizona +3.5 My Texas Tech vs. Arizona best bet is on Arizona to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Make sure to download the Action Network app for more NCAAF picks and analysis Arizona vs Texas Tech Odds Arizona vs Texas Tech point spread : Texas Tech -3.5 (-109 ), Arizona +3.5 (-112) Arizona vs Texas Tech over/under : 54.5 (-112o / -109u) Arizona vs Texas Tech moneyline : Arizona +138, Texas Tech -166 Joey McGuire and Texas Tech are once again contenders in the Big 12, coming off a Championship season a year ago, but last week's loss at Cincinnati was a bit of a reality check. The Red Raiders entered that game undefeated but have been nowhere near as dominant as they were in 2025. After falling 37-24 in a game the Bearcats dominated, they now return home sitting at 6-1 and 3-1 in conference play. This is still a good football team, particularly in Lubbock, where McGuire has built a significant home-field advantage. Texas Tech has won 12 straight at home, and McGuire is 26-5 there during his tenure. Offensively, the Red Raiders have leaned heavily on their rushing attack. Running back J'Koby Williams has been excellent, rushing for 619 yards and five touchdowns while averaging more than seven yards per carry. Texas Tech ranks 16th nationally in Rush Success Rate, and I'd expect the Red Raiders to test Arizona's front early and often. The passing attack is where I have more questions. QB Will Hammond has thrown for 1,561 yards but has just six touchdowns against six interceptions. He's made plenty of plays, but the turnovers remain concerning against an Arizona defense that has proven capable of making life difficult on opposing quarterbacks. On the other side of the ball, Texas Tech's defense is just not the same as last year's unit. They still rank 16th nationally in Rush Success Rate allowed, but the edge rushers are nowhere near the same after losing guys like David Bailey. That has led to a pass defense that has really struggled. Texas Tech ranks just 85th nationally in Pass Success Rate allowed, which is alarming in this matchup against one of the most experienced quarterbacks in the country. If the Red Raiders can't consistently make Noah Fifita uncomfortable, Arizona should have opportunities to move the football all afternoon. There are simply not enough people talking about how well Arizona is playing right now. The Wildcats sit at 6-1 and have won five straight since their only loss of the season at BYU , in a game they easily could have won. The recent results have been particularly impressive, beating Cincinnati 34-7, winning 52-31 at West Virginia, and then absolutely hammering Iowa State 39-3 last week. There is plenty of confidence within this locker room right now, and the biggest driver of that is QB Noah Fifita. I think Fifita is criminally underrated nationally. He's a flat-out winner, and in a landscape where most chase the cash and enter the portal, he deserves a ton of credit for his allegiance to Arizona. He's played a ton of football in his time in Tucson, currently sitting at 91 career touchdown passes, but this season has been particularly consistent. Fifita has thrown for 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns, and only four interceptions this year, and has total command of this offense. That experience is a big reason why I'm not too worried about the Wildcats going into a hostile environment in Lubbock. The Wildcats rank 13th nationally in Pass Success Rate, and that should give Fifita plenty of opportunities against a Texas Tech defense sitting just 85th in Pass Success Rate allowed. WR Ismail Mizell leads Arizona with 493 receiving yards and five touchdowns, while RB Quali Reescano has added five scores on the ground. I don't expect Arizona to run all over this Texas Tech defense. I do expect Fifita to be able to find matchups in the secondary and consistently move the chains through the air. Defensively, Arizona might actually be the most underrated unit in this game. The Wildcats are allowing only 16.7 points per game and rank 12th nationally in overall Success Rate allowed. More importantly for this matchup, they're 21st in Rush Success Rate allowed and 10th in Pass Success Rate allowed. That gives Arizona a legitimate answer for what Texas Tech does best. Williams and the Red Raider ground game will undoubtedly make some plays, but Arizona has consistently prevented opponents from staying ahead of schedule. If the Wildcats can make Hammond throw the football in obvious passing situations, I like their chances of forcing a mistake or two. Texas Tech is rightfully favored at home here, but I've got to take Arizona getting 3 and the hook. I think this will ultimately be a coin flip game, and I trust Fifita much more than I do Hammond in crunch time. This game obviously has major Big 12 and CFP ramifications, and both sides will prepare accordingly. The Red Raiders have been an inconsistent bunch all year, while Arizona has been steady throughout, and I want to back the more reliable team in a game of this magnitude. Give me the Wildcats as a road dog in a game I think they win outright. Bear Down. Pick: Arizona +3.5

Both have one loss and sit in a tie for second place in the competitive Big 12 standings. Texas Tech just took a surprise loss at Cincinnati and Arizona is on an impressive five-game win streak. Whoever loses this one could see their College Football Playoff ambitions vanish into thin air. Who has the ultimate advantage? How Arizona can win Sep 5, 2026; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Arizona Wildcats quarterback Noah Fifita (1) celebrates a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images Arizona has the passing-game firepower to make this a competitive matchup, but the Wildcats need to turn that strength into sustained offensive production. Noah Fifita leads an offense averaging 310.9 passing yards per game, ninth-best nationally. And this offense is third in FBS converting almost 55 percent of its third downs. Texas Tech is third-worst in the Big 12 against the pass and second-worst with 16 touchdowns allowed. Those numbers suggest the Wildcats can move the chains against this defense. The key remains protecting Fifita, establishing a running game to keep the Tech defense honest, and critically avoiding turnovers. Defensively, Arizona also needs to continue its recent success against the run. It held Iowa State to just 52 rushing yards in a 39-3 victory last week. Controlling the ground game forces the Red Raiders to throw the ball, something they're not doing all that consistently. MORE: Week 9 college football upset watch: Arizona, Clemson top road threats How Texas Tech can win Sep 26, 2026; Lubbock, Texas, USA; Texas Tech Red Raiders running back Cameron Dickey (8) rushes against Sam Houston Bearkat defensive tackle Justin Terrell (98) in the second half at Galaxy Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Balancing out this offense is crucial for the Red Raiders. Surprisingly, they rank in the bad half of the Big 12 in total offensive and defensive efficiency. The good news is they can run the ball moderately well, averaging 190 yards per game and 5 yards per carry. Running effectively helps Texas Tech control the tempo, keep Noah Fifita and Arizona's potent passing attack on the sideline, and create more manageable situations for quarterback Will Hammond. Texas Tech needs to consider giving backup quarterback Tommy Castellanos more opportunities. Score prediction for Arizona game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Things have taken quite the turn for the Texas Tech football team after suffering its first loss of the season. Getting bested by Cincinnati for 60 minutes has put the Red Raiders in a pressure point. There's little wiggle room left for Joey McGuire's team to keep its hopes of repeating as Big 12 Conference champions alive. Now they have a talented Arizona team coming to Galaxy Stadium looking to kick the Red Raiders while they're down. What will it take for Texas Tech to walk away with the win? Is Arizona actually the favorite in this game? Our breakdown of the game, plus a score prediction. What's holding Texas Tech football back? It's a layered conversation as to what is keeping the Red Raiders from reaching their potential. For starters, the offense, led by quarterback Will Hammond, hasn't put up the kind of numbers Tech fans want. Receivers have struggled to get open (besides Kenny Johnson) and when they do create separation from their defenders, Hammond hasn't found them or delivered solid throws enough to take advantage. While the rushing game has been a point of scorn for some fans, J'Koby Williams has been electric, and Cameron Dickey is on track to rejoin him in the backfield this week. Defensively, the pass defense has been sporadic. The 13 interceptions (second in the nation) and five pick-6s count, but when those haven't come, opponents have had little trouble moving the ball through the air against the Red Raiders. These things have been present all year but only came to a head against Cincinnati. Now they face an Arizona team equipped to exploit these very issues. Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense have also been operating at a high level, generating at least 280 yards through the air in six of the team's seven games. Fifita ranks third in the Big 12 with 2,064 passing yards, totaling 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions. The Wildcats have been hit with injuries to their receiving room, having already lost Tre Spivey for the season and seeing two others on the team's first availability report for the game. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Iowa Football vs. Wisconsin in the Battle for the Heartland Skip to main content SI.COM SPRING SPORTS HAWKEYENATION SI.COM HAWKEYES FB SI.COM HAWKEYES BB BASKETBALL BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS FOOTBALL NEWS While the Floyd of Rosedale slipped out of the Iowa Hawkeyes ' grasp, another trophy is on the line this week when the Wisconsin Badgers come to Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. The Battle for the Heartland trophy is going to be up for grabs. Iowa has dominated the Badgers for the last two seasons in two blowout wins, but this year looks like it will be a different type of game. These teams mirror each other quite well. Both play good defense, want to run the ball, and are winning games. It figures to be a four-quarter battle in this rivalry. Iowa holds Wisconsin under 150 yards passing This is a day when Iowa's secondary can shine, as we have seen in so many previous seasons. The group looks strong, led by Zach Lutmer. Outside, Jaylen Watson and Deshaun Lee are playing at a really high level, while Xavier Styles is growing each week at safety. Phil Parker is going to have Iowa containing Colton Joseph in the pocket, forcing him to beat Iowa with his arm. If Iowa can corral him and make him make tight-window throws all game, it's going to be a long day of incompletions and potentially some turnovers. DJ Vonnahme leads Iowa's passing game My gut tells me that Iowa's offense is going to have a very "2024" feel to it, like it did with Kaleb Johnson and all of the under-center zone runs. This is where DJ Vonnahme can feast. He can be the easy, big target for Hank Brown off of heavy play-action when the defense starts to flow. Iowa should look to Vonnahme early and often to get him the ball and set him up to run after the catch. When found in passing situations, I really like DJ Vonnahme down the seam. He can run and carry this route, plus he has the feel to find green grass between the linebackers and safeties. Iowa averages more yards per rush than Wisconsin Hear me out for one second - neither run game is going to be overly pretty in this game. Just prepare yourselves for that. These defenses are going to commit so many resources to stopping the run that even if responsibilities are messed up, there will be backup on standby to clean up the mess. I think Iowa's defense is going to eliminate much of the success for Wisconsin by containing Colton Joseph, which is a specialty of Phil Parker, and therefore force the backs to make something happen. Iowa can stop the run in its base defense, which it should be in for most of this game. Offensively, it won't be pretty for Iowa, but I think the Hawkeyes have a spirited run game that converts some ugly short-yardage plays and stays patient enough to get a few chunks from the running back room. It will take time, but Iowa's run game gets going just enough in this one. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Brad Schultz Fri, October 30, 2026 at 5:03 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kirk Ferentz's perspective of the Iowa-Wisconsin rivalry When Iowa football fans glanced at the 2026 schedule in the summer, one of the games that they chalked up as likely wins was a Halloween contest against rival Wisconsin. And it made perfect sense back then. The Badger program was seemingly going nowhere under head coach Luke Fickell, and many people believed 2026 would be Fickell's final season before the school would cut ties with him. But flash-forward to Halloween, and Iowa and Wisconsin enter this matchup in completely different directions. The Hawkeyes are desperate for a bounce-back win after an ugly loss at Minnesota last weekend, while the Badgers could vault themselves into College Football Playoff contention with a victory (just check their schedule after the Iowa game). Every Iowa-Wisconsin game always seems to provide something unusual, so one can only imagine what will happen on Saturday. Here's my prediction for the matchup. Matchup: No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers (5-2, 3-1) @ Iowa Hawkeyes (5-2, 2-2) Location: Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa Scheduled game time: Oct. 31 at 11:10 a.m. Weather: 63 degrees Announcers: Gus Johnson (play-by-play), Joel Klatt (analyst), Jenny Taft (sideline) Radio: Hawkeye Radio Network (Gary Dolphin, Pat Angerer) Student Radio: KRUI (Collin Carrithers, Luke Jorden) I'm very surprised that Wisconsin is a competitive team at this point, but Iowa Everywhere's Chris Hassel said it best on Wednesday - the Badgers know their identity by now and the Hawkeyes don't. Iowa essentially using a roulette wheel to determine its starting quarterback each week has clearly caused this offense to be inconsistent week in and week out. Though Wisconsin hasn't received great quarterback play from Old Dominion transfer Colton Joseph, it has relied on a good run game and excellent defense to win football games. Sticking to that strategy has worked well for the Badgers. All you have to do to figure that out is go back and watch their last game against USC. Wisconsin dominated both lines of scrimmage en route to a 24-7 victory last weekend and you better believe they'll try and do the same thing to Iowa. But can the Badgers actually come to Kinnick Stadium and pull this one out? The momentum is definitely on Wisconsin's side of the ball, but if there's one edge Iowa has, it's the fact that it's playing at Kinnick Stadium. The Badgers haven't won in Iowa City since 2018, with the Hawkeyes winning the last three games in Kinnick by a combined score of 94-27. I don't expect a lot of points to be scored in this one (stay tuned for my betting prediction later today), but if there's one thing I know about Kirk Ferentz, it's his ability to win these Big Ten grinders. He's going to try and flip the calendar back to 2023 and win this game with complimentary football. That wouldn't be a good strategy on the road, but I think this defense will feed off the home crowd and give their offense enough short fields to secure a narrow victory. The Hawkeyes take down Wisconsin for the sixth time in seven games. Prediction: Iowa 16, Wisconsin 13

away.blurb: This is hardly how Nelson would have scripted his career. He signed with the Badgers out of Stoughton High School, following in the footsteps of his dad, Todd, who lettered for the Badgers from 1986-88 and his brother Jack , who started on the offensive line for four seasons (2021-24). The major setbacks were the patellar tendon injury, which happened during winter conditioning before last season. Then just as he was ramping up for a return, he required back surgery before spring practice this year. “The doubts do creep into your mind, but I've got to give all the blessings to [strength] coach Brady [Collins], Coach Mateos, the training room,” Nelson said. “They really keep your mind from going into a dark spot like that. I always felt motivated to try and make my return.” He sat out all of spring practice but returned to the field late in fall camp. “You can just see him practice every day. He's just hungry to play the game," Heywood said. "He's hungry to play and wants to get out there. If the coaches see that, they have no option but to put him on the field.” Beyond the resiliency to return from injury, the interesting part of Nelson's resurgence is that it came at guard instead of tackle. Guard is a position he never played in a game, as far as he can remember. Getting Nelson into the mix has helped UW endure a stretch when center Austin Kawecki, the starter for the first five games, has been out with a broken hand. That injury caused the coaches to move junior Stylz Blackmon from right guard to center. "I thought I played well," Nelson said. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Not that it matters by any means, but aside from its impressive road win against Georgia two weeks ago, nothing particularly jumps off the page to me about Alex Golesh’s first team at Auburn. That’s not to say Golesh isn’t the right fit for the job either. He has the Tigers sitting above .500 and is working through his first season as a head coach at a Power Four program. As it pertains to the game itself, I expect Ole Miss to maintain its home win streak that dates back to September of the 2024 season. This certainly should be a focused group after picking up its second loss in Texas last weekend and they can’t afford to overlook Auburn even though Georgia is around the corner. Controlling their playoff destiny is on thin ice. Trinidad Chambliss could use a bounce back game after not looking like himself the past two weeks. Considering Auburn’s weaker pass defense through its secondary, I believe Chambliss does what he desperately needs to do and may even incorporate his legs more than usual. Ole Miss needs to prove it can find a faster start on the offensive side of the ball as a whole. Defensively, Ole Miss should match up well against an offense that has already surrendered 29 sacks (4.3 per game) if the unit can contain Byrum Brown. The Tigers’ quarterback leads the team in rushing yards, but still looks like a signal-caller in his first season in the SEC. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 17 While Auburn is more than capable of pulling off the upset, just look at its victory over No. 3 Georgia in Athens, I don’t see it happening this Saturday. Against Texas, the Ole Miss offense did everything it could to let Texas pull away. However, despite struggling for most of the night, they lost the game by just seven points. The two games prior to Texas, Ole Miss won by blowing out its opponents. With the Rebels’ back against the wall and needing to go on a win streak if they want to make the College Football Playoff, I think they win easily against Auburn and carry some nice momentum into their matchup against the Georgia Bulldogs next Saturday night. Ole Miss 34, Auburn 17 Cooper Ferguson Alex Golesh will take this Auburn team to greener pastures than Hugh Freeze ever did, and I think that in the alternate universe where Golesh came to Auburn, things worked out. A great coach tasked with waking a sleeping giant, I think Auburn will, in due time, become a force to be reckoned with again in the SEC. That time is not now, though. Florida and the first half against Texas need to be remembered as blips in a strong season for the Rebels in years to come. With a strong showing against Auburn this Halloween, Ole Miss will be well on its way to correcting its path. Chambliss and Co. dispatch the Tigers easily, and Ole Miss moves on to prep for Georgia. Ole Miss 49, Auburn 14 Billy Flowers Byrum Brown will be a major problem for the Ole Miss run defense, but Auburn's offensive line is horrific. I think the Tigers' only path to victory is through Brown's legs, which, frankly, will not put enough points on the board for Auburn. I think Trinidad bounces back, and Makhai Frazier has a breakout performance against the Tiger's less-than-stellar rush defense. I do think Auburn can keep the game close, thanks to their rushing attack. The Ole Miss offense is too talented, and the Tigers won't score enough to match it. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 27 Zion Trammell Ole Miss is coming off a disappointing performance against Texas and really needs a solid response this week. The key to victory is to keep Byrum Brown in the pocket. The Auburn quarterback can make big plays with his legs, so limiting his mobility will be a priority. The Tigers knocked off Georgia a couple of weeks ago, but I think Pete Golding’s team responds well at home. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24 The Ole Miss Rebels face a must-win game against the Auburn Tigers. They won't disappoint. Auburn is a dangerous football team, but Ole Miss will show its talent when it needs to. Trinidad Chambliss will have a day as the defense struggles at first but settles in. The Rebels, in the end, will win this game by three-plus touchdowns. Ole Miss 45, Auburn 24 Published 22 hours ago TYLER KOMIS Bio: Tyler Komis is a beat reporter for Ole Miss On SI. Who does ESPN have winning when Auburn travels to Ole Miss on Saturday? According to the ESPN Matchup Predictor , Auburn has a 25.1% chance of picking up a victory at Ole Miss. The Tigers have not lost back-to-back games this season and will be looking to avoid that in Oxford, Mississippi, on Saturday. It will be a tall task for Auburn to come away with a win over the Rebels, who are coming off a narrow defeat last week at the hands of the Texas Longhorns . Ole Miss almost made a huge comeback after trailing Texas 24-3 at halftime. Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss could not find the end zone as time expired, and Ole Miss lost 34-27. At 5-2, Ole Miss can not afford another loss if they want to make the College Football Playoff. This will be the first meeting between the two schools since the 2023 season , when Ole Miss defeated Auburn in the first year of the Hugh Freeze era. These two programs met each year when they were both part of the SEC West division. Auburn leads the all-time series 35-12, but Ole Miss has won the last two meetings. In the final five games of the season, Auburn should be able to snap their streak of five consecutive losing seasons. With four wins, Auburn should be able to get three more victories with games against Arkansas, Mississippi State, and Samford. A matchup that could help Auburn pull off an upset victory over Ole Miss is in the run game. The Rebels are at the bottom of the SEC, giving up 161.1 yards per game on the ground. Saturday could be an opportunity for Byrum Brown and the Auburn running backs to have a big game. That's important for an Auburn offense that has struggled to establish the running game. Jeremiah Cobb and Omar Mabson could have opportunities to make plays, while quarterback Byrum Brown could also find success running the football. Ole Miss has also struggled against the pass, allowing 27 completions of at least 20 yards this season. If Auburn can take advantage of those weaknesses, the Tigers could have one of their better offensive performances. But Auburn's defense remains a major concern. While Ole Miss has struggled defensively, Auburn hasn't been much better. The Tigers allowed 552 total yards against LSU, including 387 passing yards and three touchdowns from quarterback Sam Leavitt. Now Auburn faces another dangerous quarterback in Trinidad Chambliss. Chambliss has the ability to extend plays with his legs and create explosive plays downfield. And considering Auburn's struggles in the secondary, that could be a major problem. Even if Auburn's offense improves, the Tigers still have to find a way to slow down Ole Miss. Auburn cannot afford another slow start. The Tigers trailed LSU 31-10 at halftime and never recovered. away.headline: Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gives key injury update on Tai Buster
away.blurb: Sophomore Tai Buster was expected to be a key piece of Auburn's offensive line rotation this season, but a preseason setback has kept him away from the field . This week, Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gave a positive report for Buster's availability, saying he could be available to play as early as a few weeks. “Tai (Buster) has worked his tail off. I give Tai a lot of credit. He is working through return to play," Golesh said Monday. "The hope is that here in a couple of weeks, we get him fully integrated in practice, and it gives us a chance to see where he is." For injured players, it can take days or weeks to catch up and return to their routine, but Golesh says that will not be the case for Buster. Buster has remained immersed in practice and should return to full speed quickly. "He’s been engaged; I give him a lot of credit again, he’s been engaged," Golesh said. "He’s itching to get back out there. I thought when he got banged up, he was competing at a high level. We’re excited to get him back here soon.” Adding Buster to the rotation will not solve every issue the offensive line faces, but having an extra body will help keep linemen, especially at guard, fresh during Auburn's final stretch of regular-season games. The Tigers will be without Buster for their next game, Saturday at Ole Miss, but he could return in November to assist Auburn with their pursuit of bowl eligibility. The Rebels rank last in the SEC in rushing defense, allowing 161.1 yards per game. Texas rushed for 207 yards against Ole Miss, while Florida's top two running backs combined for 268 yards. That's important for an Auburn offense that has struggled to establish the running game. Jeremiah Cobb and Omar Mabson could have opportunities to make plays, while quarterback Byrum Brown could also find success running the football. Ole Miss has also struggled against the pass, allowing 27 completions of at least 20 yards this season. If Auburn can take advantage of those weaknesses, the Tigers could have one of their better offensive performances. But Auburn's defense remains a major concern. While Ole Miss has struggled defensively, Auburn hasn't been much better. The Tigers allowed 552 total yards against LSU, including 387 passing yards and three touchdowns from quarterback Sam Leavitt. Now Auburn faces another dangerous quarterback in Trinidad Chambliss. Chambliss has the ability to extend plays with his legs and create explosive plays downfield. And considering Auburn's struggles in the secondary, that could be a major problem. Even if Auburn's offense improves, the Tigers still have to find a way to slow down Ole Miss. Auburn cannot afford another slow start. The Tigers trailed LSU 31-10 at halftime and never recovered. Against Ole Miss, Auburn needs to establish the running game early, avoid negative plays, and keep the game competitive. The Rebels will also be without several players, including star running back Kewan Lacy and multiple defensive backs. That could create opportunities for Auburn. But the Tigers still have to take advantage. Auburn's victory over Georgia showed what can happen when Golesh's team plays well and forces turnovers. And Ole Miss has shown it can be vulnerable, particularly defensively. But Auburn will need a much better performance than what it showed against LSU, especially defensively

With Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium under renovation until August 2028, the setting will be different. The stakes remain the same. In fact, there may be an even higher degree of intensity to this year's showdown between the border foes because of the circumstances. It's the first time since 2020 that both are ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC) is coming off a bye week after a stunning home loss to Auburn , and Florida (5-2, 3-2) is riding high off an Oct. 17 road win over Texas. First-year Gators coach Jon Sumrall already has two wins over top-10 teams (Ole Miss and Texas) and could get his team firmly in the College Football Playoff hunt with another marquee win. The Bulldogs have won five straight meetings in the series, but Sumrall has reinvigorated the Florida program this season since arriving from Tulane. The Gators have shown the ability to slay some of the SEC's top dogs already this season, and Georgia will need to be on high alert to avoid suffering consecutive regular season losses for the first time since Kirby Smart's first season in 2015. Georgia vs. Florida: Need to know Florida's quarterback situation: Starting in place of the injured Aaron Philo, Florida sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. rose to the occasion in a Week 7 win at Texas. The inexperienced quarterback completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions against the Longhorns' vaunted defense while also totaling 41 rushing yards. But will he play against Georgia? Philo was listed as questionable on the Gators' first student-athlete availability report this week, raising questions over who will get the nod under center. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he doesn't plan to name a starter before the game, which will force Georgia to prepare for both QBs. Jones is more mobile, but he's also put his full repertoire on tape now. Philo is still dealing with a right shoulder injury, but he did practice this week. Georgia's run defense: Regardless of who starts at quarterback for Florida, the Gators are going to try and lean on their run game. Georgia's run defense has shown some vulnerability in the past two games. Led by quarterback Byrum Brown, Auburn totaled 192 yards rushing against the Bulldogs in an Oct. 17 upset road win over UGA. The week before, Alabama amassed 161 yards on the ground against Georgia. Up until those two games, Georgia's run defense had been stout. Facing Florida might be the toughest test yet of Georgia's ability to stop the run. The Gators raced to a 4-0 start, including wins over Auburn and Ole Miss, by rushing for 200+ yards in each game. The UF rushing game has been less effective in three games since then, but star back Jadan Baugh is a load to handle. He leads the SEC in rushing touchdowns with 13 and is third in rushing yards with 763. CFP implications: Georgia's chances of reaching the College Football Playoff will rise to 94.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. Those odds would dip to 72.7% with a loss. Entering Saturday, Florida has just a 9.5% chance to make it, but that mark would surge to 29% with an upset win over the Bulldogs. On the flip side, suffering a third loss would leave UF with just a 5.6% chance of making the playoff. If the Gators suffer a third loss against Georgia, they would need to run the table against Oklahoma, Kentucky, Vanderbilt and Florida State and then get some help from other teams to have any shot at reaching the field with a 9-3 record. Florida will have the Bulldogs' full attention after an upset win at Texas, and UGA won't be remotely caught off guard by anything the Gators attempt offensively. Georgia's defensive staff knows Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner well. On the opposite side, the Gators have shown they are vulnerable on defense, and Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton will be playing with a chip on his shoulder after a rare poor performance against Auburn. picks.blurb: Three Bold Prediction's for Georgia Football's Showdown with Florida in Atlanta Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Florida Gators in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party , except this time it may take place indoors. While EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville undergoes renovation, the game is taking a two game hiatus from Duval County. The game will take place in Mercedes-Benz stadium in Atlanta on Saturday. Depending on the weather, the roof could be closed, hence the party being inside. This will be a very different atmosphere for this historic rivalry. Now, Florida fans will see that Jacksonville is not that neutral of a site. Atlanta is the equivalent in Georgia. So, that means some ridiculous things could happen Saturday afternoon. Here are three bold predictions for Saturday: Gunner Stockton Totals 4 Touchdowns Gunner Stockton is coming off of the worst game of his life, where he turned the ball over three times for the first time in his career, including the untimely fumble at the end of the game. That fumble led to Auburn’s game-winning field goal. Florida has the second worst passing defense in the SEC. Stockton is one of the best and most efficient quarterbacks in the nation. A bounce back game seems likely, and he will total at least four scores. Georgia Wins Turnover Margin by 2 The Dawgs lost the turnover battle to Auburn 0-3, and they almost won. Georgia has been better about creating turnover opportunities this year than it was last season. Georgia has also had a knack for winning games despite losing the turnover battle. This game last year is an example of that. Georgia is due for a big turnover game. The Dawgs only have two takeaways over the last three games. Jadan Baugh Gets His Jadan Baugh is arguably college football’s best running back. He has simmered down since his 600-yard and 11-touchdown start over the first four games. Rushing for over 90 yards and a score en route to an upset road win over Texas can be considered a bounce back. Georgia’s run defense has progressively gotten worse as the season has gone on. Alabama was able to rip off some expl;osive and total about 160 yards on the ground. Byrum Brown ran all over the Dawgs, helping Auburn total over 190 rushing yards. Baugh is good enough to get his. Georgia is good enough to win even if that happens. I think he will have around 100 total yards and a score. picks.blurb: Odds Have Changed for Georgia Football vs. Florida Gators Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS ATHENS - Odds have been updated to Georgia Football’s massive clash with the Florida Gators 48 hours before the rivals face off in Atlanta. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. For the first time in the history of the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party, Florida and Georgia will play in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with kickoff slated for Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). The Bulldogs are 11.5-point favorites, and my Florida vs. Georgia prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's team to take advantage of Jon Sumrall's defense in his first Cocktail Party. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. While he's just 5-4 against the spread in those games, his Bulldogs have the advantage against a sporadic Florida team. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. home.blurb: The most glaring of the ailments listed Wednesday evening are those that Florida’s quarterbacks suffer from heading into Saturday. Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. both made their way onto the list, with each’s status deemed as questionable heading into the Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic. Philo is named on the availability report for the second straight game week following a shoulder injury late in the loss to South Carolina. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed UF's last three games with a knee strain, is listed as probable. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said both practiced this week and hinted Jones was dealing with issues following the Texas win during his opening week press conference on October 26. If Jones and Philo both can't go, Florida would turn to its third-string quarterback, redshirt junior Aidan Warner, or true freshman Will Griffin. Warner appeared in the Florida-Georgia game in 2024 when DJ Lagway went down with a hamstring injury and made one career start the following week at Texas. picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Oct 24, 2026; Evanston, Illinois, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) runs with the ball against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at New Ryan Field. Credit: David Banks- | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Northwestern’s rushing attack has also been a major part of its offensive success, led by the dynamic running back duo of Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II, who have combined for over 900 rushing yards this season. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. Despite Dante Moore’s potential absence the rest of the season, Northwestern will still face a tough challenge on the road against a talented Oregon team. Quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have shared playing time the past three games for the Ducks. Raiola struggled in last weekend’s loss to Illinois, completing 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards, as the defeat dealt a major blow to Oregon’s hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff for a third consecutive season. Oct 24, 2026; Champaign, Illinois, USA; Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola (8) passes the ball as Illinois Fighting Illini linebacker Ismael Kante (26) defends during the second half at Gies Memorial Stadium. Credit: Ron Johnson- | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Following the loss, Oregon made changes to its coaching staff, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Following the loss, Oregon made changes to its coaching staff, firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Mehringer had been promoted to the role at the start of the season after Will Stein departed to become the head coach at Kentucky, but his tenure was ultimately short-lived. This weekend’s matchup will be just the third time that both teams will be meeting, and the first time that they will match up at Autzen Stadium. They have split results, with Oregon taking the most recent matchup last season. Stay up to date on the Wildcats by bookmarking Northwestern On SI and follow us on Twitter. Published Oct 27, 2026 GABRIELLA EGOZI Gabriella Egozi is an accomplished journalism student at Northwestern University’s Medill School of Journalism, passionate about sports media, writing, and broadcasting. She was born and raised in Miami, Florida, thus her passion for sports reporting originated from watching the Miami HEAT in the NBA Bubble. Gabriella has had experiences working as an intern for the digital team at NBC6 and Telemundo 51, as well as with CBS Sports at live sporting events, including the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament. Gabriella most recently was an intern at CNN on NewsNight with Abby Phillip in New York, assisting with production and content creation roles. At Northwestern, Gabriella serves as a sideline reporter, color analyst, writer and play-by-play commentator for Big Ten sporting events. Gabriella is a reporter for WNUR Sports, NNN Sports Night, The Daily Northwestern and BigTen Network StudentU Productions. Gabriella wants to pursue a career within sports media and hopes to continue to further propel her passions for storytelling and connecting communities through her work. Game preview, prediction, betting line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NBA Cup: Friday roundup Steph breaks Luka's ankles NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Ryan Clarke Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:29 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Seeking to climb out of the low point of its 2026 season, Oregon football returns home on Halloween to host No. 20 Northwestern. Legendary Oregon coach Chip Kelly is calling plays on the opposite sideline as the Wildcats' offensive coordinator, and Dan Lanning will rely on interim play-caller Jay Johnson to run his offense following the firing of Drew Mehringer. Can the Ducks get their minds right and put together a convincing performance on both sides of the ball for a win over a ranked team? Here is a full preview: Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) vs. No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 12:30 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium, Eugene Latest line: Oregon by 3.5 points Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game streaming only on Peacock (costs just $12.99/month). There is no traditional cable TV broadcast for this game as it is one of several Peacock-exclusive Big Ten football matchups that will appear on NBC's streaming platform. Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. A RUNNING THREAT Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles has been to Autzen Stadium before. The former Oregon State and Michigan State signal-caller is having a career year, completing 71.3% of his passes for 1,617 yards, 12 touchdowns and one interception. Chiles is also a serious threat with his legs, rushing for nine touchdowns this season. That versatility could cause the Oregon defense problems, particularly with how creative Kelly is getting with the Northwestern offense. The Ducks' game plan starts and ends with getting pressure on Chiles and keeping him contained in the run game as well. The Wildcats are No. 35 in the country at 34.7 points per game. For all the dominance Oregon's defense has shown despite the struggles of its offense, this Northwestern team has the best and most balanced offense of any team the Ducks have faced these past four weeks. Oregon's quarterback situation remains up in the air after another poor performance from Dylan Raiola against Illinois. While the Nebraska transfer has had his moments this season, his play in two losses to UCLA and Illinois raises serious cause for concern. Enter sophomore Akili Smith Jr., the son of the former Oregon quarterback, who some fans are clamoring for to start this week. He has a big arm and all the physical traits one could want at the position, but is he ready to face a fearsome Northwestern defense? The answer to that question will determine whether Lanning and company decide to hand the keys to Oregon's flailing offense over to Smith. If the Ducks still think they are better off with a veteran presence in Raiola, despite his struggles, that will delay Smith's starting debut. But it's hard to imagine Oregon's quarterback play being any worse, so, why not give it a shot? GETTING PLAYMAKERS BACK Oregon should have three of its top wide receivers back against Northwestern who missed the Illinois game: Evan Stewart, Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Stewart was dealing with an injury that kept him out of the Nebraska game, after which he was arrested on suspicion of DUII. And the reason for Hampton and Lott's absence on the trip to Champaign is unknown, though Lanning did not note any specific injury. Whoever starts at quarterback for Oregon will benefit from a full complement of receivers, save for the injured Jeremiah McClellan. Northwestern gets a crucial player back this week, too: tight end Luke Dehnicke no longer appears on the injury report. He had a massive performance last time he took the field against Indiana on Sept. 25, hauling in seven passes for 140 yards. A lot of the things that we ask our players to do are things I don't think grown men do well, right? When it's good, there's a level of energy and effort. (Photo by Zoe Davis/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inside NU Archives Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:40 PM UTC · 10 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern has played itself into College Football Playoff contention. The 'Cats sit as the No. 20-ranked team in the nation, with six wins over South Dakota State, Colorado, Penn State, Michigan State, Ball State and Rutgers, and a narrow 29-23 loss on the road to the now No. 4-ranked Indiana Hoosiers. Thus far this season, they've passed the eye test, wowing pundits around the country with creative offensive formations and a turnover happy defense, but they are in need of quality wins over top-notch opponents. Over the next four weeks, NU will get three chances to secure resumé-changing victories, with matchups booked against Oregon, Iowa, Ohio State and Minnesota. The first of which, against Dan Lanning's Ducks, will take place on Saturday. Here's the INU staff's predictions for the 'Cats' road test against the 4-3 Oregon Ducks: Charlie Jacobs (27-16 Northwestern ) This Northwestern team has a different vibe to it. Although the Wildcats' last road trip was too close for comfort, Oregon has been struggling a lot lately and offers the perfect opportunity for Northwestern to pick up the win. Whether it's Brock Thomas or Dylan Raiola at quarterback, I'm not sure the Ducks can keep up with the Wildcats' offense, which will likely score enough no matter what. Plus, Chip Kelly back calling plays in Autzen… there's very few storylines better than that this week. Oregon, while a very talented roster, hasn't been able to put it all together. Even with a new offensive coordinator this week (or lack thereof), Oregon's offense has to prove it can compete for it to be threatening, even if the weapons are healthy. I'm taking the 'Cats. Jackson Pick (24-13 Northwestern ) Northwestern enters the meat of its schedule on a four-game winning streak, and at face value it's hard not to favor the 'Cats here. Aidan Chiles collected five total touchdowns against Rutgers on Saturday, with Caleb Komolafe adding one of his own to go with his 150 rushing yards on the day. Oregon, one of the preseason national championship favorites, has lost two of its last three, including a 21-10 shocker at Illinois that knocked it out of College Football Playoff contention. One reason for the Ducks' slide is obvious: their quarterback and potential No. 1-overall pick Dante Moore suffered a head injury against USC, and neither Dylan Raiola nor Brock Thomas have been able to sufficiently replace his production — Oregon has gone from 304 passing yards per game to just 205 since Moore's injury. On Saturday, Moore's continued absence will once again stifle an Oregon offense whose rushing attack hasn't produced enough to supplement its weakened passing game. While its defense has been stout enough, Northwestern will travel to Eugene with the strongest offense the Ducks have faced since their Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State. This game – if the Wildcats can win it – will begin to put the CFP in their sights. Autzen Stadium is a raucous environment to travel to for a NU team that's struggled on the road, and this is easily their biggest test since traveling to face Indiana. Unlike with the Hoosiers, though, the 'Cats don't need to execute at 100% to take this one. On another big day for the Wildcats' defense, Chiles will do just enough to escape Autzen with a season-defining victory. Donovan West (21-17 Oregon ) Five punts, three missed field goals and a fumble. That's how eight of Oregon's drives ended against Illinois last week. It was a masterclass in miscues from head coach Dan Lanning and the Ducks in a disappointing result that marked a season that has spun out of control. Despite a roster made up mostly of four- and five-star recruits, Oregon is 4-3 and has proven that raw talent doesn't automatically make a good football team. Northwestern, however, has proven the opposite. The 'Cats are an injury-ridden team of misfits that has united around a common goal and beaten the breaks off of three power conference teams. The only problem for NU is that its dominance has made the games boring to watch and has led to the Wildcat Wall leaving early.​ Yet, with the two programs on opposite trajectories, Oregon will still walk onto its home field on Saturday as favorites. The sports books trust the Ducks' depth and talent, and so do I. Their victories over USC and Nebraska, two wins more impressive than anything Northwestern has done, show that Oregon can still be a good football team. The Ducks will trot into Autzen Stadium knowing they need to win for any chance at making the playoff and grind their way to victory with a dominant performance in the trenches. As it did against Indiana, Northwestern will struggle to run the ball against Oregon, and Aidan Chiles won't be able to get it done through the air. The 'Cats' dreamy season will take a reality check, and expectations will be reevaluated. Zac Penson (24-17 Oregon ) I want to be wrong. The biggest hump I struggle to get over is that Oregon still has a stellar defense. Despite losing Dante Moore for the year, their experience and poise on defense is something they have continued to show over the past few weeks, allowing only 17 points to UCLA and just 14 points to Nebraska. Northwestern has also seemed to struggle on the road this season, falling to Indiana and squeaking out a win over Michigan State. And this stadium will be louder. Coming in at No. 20 on the AP Poll against an unranked Oregon team, the Wildcats have something to prove. Oregon lost to Illinois last week, so they clearly aren't invincible, but that was in Champaign. Autzen Stadium is a whole different animal. Despite losing to Illinois, Oregon is indeed favored. I would love to see the Cardiac 'Cats pull off the upset on this one, but I believe the pressure of the moment is only mounting for the Wildcats as the days drag on and they board their flight to Eugene. I believe Northwestern won't go down without a fight, though, and I expect this one to be a fun battle to the end. Whitley Williams (24-21 Northwestern ) Blurb: Strike while the opponent is weak. Northwestern is seeking its fifth consecutive win against the Oregon Ducks. Once considered a College Football Playoff contender, Oregon has endured a series of unexpected setbacks. The Ducks fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following their loss to Illinois. Once known for their explosive offense and "Pac-12 After Dark" spectacles, the Ducks are now a team searching for their identity. In many ways, the roles have reversed. Northwestern boasts a creative, explosive offense that keeps opposing defenses guessing. Offensive coordinator Chip Kelly will need to lean on that trickery against an elite Oregon defense that allows just 3.65 yards per carry and 197.6 passing yards a game. Assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson will call the plays for Oregon on Saturday. With Dante Moore out for the season, Oregon will start Dylan Raiola at quarterback. Against Illinois, Raiola completed 66% of his passes for 246 yards but couldn't finish the job. The Wildcats will have to lock down deep-threat wide receiver Dakorien Moore. Aidan Chiles has played extremely tough on the road in hostile environments, and this test in Eugene will certainly show what the Wildcats are truly made of. Kussh Mital (21-10 Northwestern ) I don't see why this game should be any different than Oregon's previous matchup against Illinois. I believe this so much that I am predicting that same score in the Wildcats favor. Oregon's defense is great, don't get me wrong, but they just gave up over 200 rushing yards to Illinois, and Northwestern has a flat out better rushing attack. Moreover, Northwestern can air the ball out much more efficiently, something the Ducks have not had to deal with in a couple weeks. Aidan Chiles is the best quarterback Oregon has faced since Jayden Maiava, who threw for over 300 yards and two touchdown passes against it. Chiles probably won't do that, but he will certainly do some damage. However, the main issue for this Oregon squad is the quarterback position. When you can't trust your quarterback to run the offense effectively, it's hard to expect to win the game. Even with the return of some of the receivers for Oregon, Dylan Raiola is not going to get the job done against Northwestern. With the Wildcats somehow entering the game as underdogs, I expect them to wear that title with honor and make Oregon fans extra fearful on Halloween. Drew Christmann (23-16 Northwestern ) Since Dante Moore went down with a scary and controversial injury against USC, Oregon has a simple problem: they can't score. Since that Week 4 matchup in LA, the Ducks have scored no more than 17 points a game, down from 47.5 in prior games, including an 84-0 shutout against Portland. Now, after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer following a loss to Illinois last week, in which the Ducks scored just 10 points, it's unclear what Oregon's offense will look like going forward, with Dan Lanning confirming he doesn't expect Moore to return for the rest of the season. Northwestern is the opposite. After years of a less-than-optimal offense, the Wildcats have been one of the conference's best, especially on the ground, where they average 204.6 yards per game. Aidan Chiles has been no slouch in the air, too, throwing for 1,617 yards with a 71.3% completion rate and just one interception. That, along with Chip Kelly's return to Autzen, makes for a scary matchup for Oregon. The ideal situation for the 'Cats' is a quick start, as it did against Rutgers last week, when they scored on the first three possessions of the game. But Northwestern has shown they know how to play from behind in hostile environments, like in Bloomington, where they scored 16 points in the final quarter to push defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the brink and at Michigan State in East Lansing, where Chiles drove 64 yards against his former school to win on a game-winning kick. The Wildcats have shown they can win both ways, and against an Oregon team whose season is spiraling, I see Northwestern moving to 7-1 on Halloween. Adam Sutro (27-24 Northwestern ) I have low confidence in Northwestern's defense entering this football game. A poor Rutgers offense killed the 'Cats on the ground last week, exposing a run defense issue that has been a problem all year for Northwestern. Fortunately for the 'Cats, Oregon has operated more through the air than on the ground for most of the season… though I think with all the talent the Ducks have on their offensive line, they will figure out how to expose the 'Cats' run defense and move the ball. Northwestern’s defense will need to communicate effectively and limit explosive plays as Oregon adjusts to a new offensive play-caller . Brendan Flakes is listed as doubtful, while Robby Preckel remains questionable. Flakes has contributed on special teams, including blocking a key field goal in Northwestern’s win over Michigan State . His potential absence could affect the Wildcats’ special teams depth against Oregon. Several other players remain out, including offensive lineman Ezomo Oratokhai, Josh Fussell, Daniel Anderson, Max Mohring, Jason Reynolds II, Callen Campbell, Qayvier Johnson, Jacob Miller and Chris Petrucci. Braxton Strong is also listed as out after previously being listed as doubtful. With several players still sidelined, Northwestern will need contributions from across its roster. Dehnicke’s potential return would provide a welcome boost, while the defense must find ways to compensate for Fitzgerald’s absence as the Wildcats look to extend their winning streak. home.headline: Oregon Ducks players react to losing Dante Moore for the season: ‘It was bad news to hear’
home.blurb: EUGENE — The Oregon Ducks started life in a new normal this week when hopes of quarterback Dante Moore ’s return were extinguished. RELATED : Experts release new Oregon-Northwestern predictions, picks and best bets after Dante Moore officially ruled out for season For four weeks since Moore was struck in the head while sliding to end a run during a 41-27 win at USC, the team watched him return to practice and hoped he would play again. The offense scored just 42 points over the three games he missed. “It was very heartbreaking to hear, but at the same time, we’ve kind of been getting used to other quarterbacks playing,” he said. “So, in terms of football plays and stuff like that, we just got to rock out with what we’ve been doing. So, we’re already used to it, but I feel for him deeply.” This week, the Ducks also fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. His biggest failing was not generating enough offense with a marginal and unsettled offensive line. Dante Moore was also out. Plus, in two games, the Ducks were missing the team’s top two wide receivers, Jeremiah McClellan and Evan Stewart. At Illinois, the Ducks were missing four of their top five wide receivers. Stream : You watch this game streaming only on Peacock (costs just $12.99/month). There is no traditional cable TV broadcast for this game as it is one of several Peacock-exclusive Big Ten football matchups that will appear on NBC’s streaming platform. Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. Coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore would miss the remainder of the season . Moore missed three games after entering concussion protocol following a vicious hit to the head on Sept. 26 at USC. The news, relayed to the team on Sunday, left several players devastated as Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) prepares to host No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) on Saturday. “It was bad news to hear,” Oregon senior tight end Jamari Johnson said. “That was my guy.” Saturday’s 21-10 loss at Illinois pretty much ended the Ducks’ realistic hope of reaching the College Football Playoff. The next day, Moore told the team he wouldn’t be returning to the field. “Of course, that’s something that’s very heartbreaking, being that he was the first guy to even speak to me when I first got here,” sophomore wide receiver Dakorien Moore said. “We got the same last name, to give us even more connection. So, just that bond that we have in general, I feel for him.” Dante Moore led the Ducks to the national semifinals last season, where they lost to Indiana. Soon after, Moore returned to Oregon to develop and chase a national title — a decision Johnson recalled with both fondness and sadness. “That was like one of the first flashbacks I had in my mind when he said (he was done for the season),” Johnson said. “So, it’s my dog, man.
