The Gamecocks' success is primarily due to their rushing offense that averages an SEC-best 218.3 yards per game. It's been a combination of running back Matt Fuller and quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the ground. Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns. Sellers is right behind him with 507 yards and four touchdowns. The Sooners' offense is bogged down by its SEC-worst run game, but the passing game has also had its ups and downs. John Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards at a 66.7% completion rate with 11 touchdowns to seven interceptions, tied for the second most in the SEC. Wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III has the sixth-most receiving yards in the SEC with 578 and three touchdowns Although the Sooners have faced plenty of challenges offensively, their defense has played well, ranking second in the SEC in total yards allowed and first in pass defense. Part of their ability to defend well against the pass is their pass rush that's gotten 22 sacks, which ties for third in the SEC. South Carolina vs Oklahoma scouting report Why South Carolina has an advantage: Even though Oklahoma's defense is its strength, against the run, the Sooners haven't been as formidable as they are against the pass. They allow an average of 117.4 rushing yards, ranking eighth in the SEC. This favors a South Carolina team that gains most of its yards on the ground. As for facing the Sooners' pressure on passing plays, the Gamecocks' offensive line has held its own, allowing 15 sacks, tied for sixth in the SEC. Sellers' mobility will also be an asset in allowing him to escape the pocket and break free on scrambles, in addition to his designed runs. Why Oklahoma has an advantage: The Sooners have struggled to score but now face a bottom-five SEC defense in points allowed. Mateer could have an easier time settling into a rhythm against the Gamecocks, who give up 222.7 passing yards per game and have just four interceptions. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. EDT on SEC Network. Oklahoma is favored by -5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -200. The total is set at 44.5 points. Here's my South Carolina vs. Oklahoma prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 31, 2026. South Carolina vs. Oklahoma Pick: South Carolina 1st Quarter ML (+106, FanDuel) My Oklahoma vs. South Carolina best bet is on South Carolina to lead after the first quarter. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. South Carolina vs Oklahoma Odds South Carolina vs Oklahoma point spread : Oklahoma -5 (-108 ), S. Carolina +5 (-115) South Carolina vs Oklahoma over/under : 44.5 (-110o / -110u) South Carolina vs Oklahoma moneyline : S. Carolina +164, Oklahoma -200 South Carolina is the hotter of the two teams, and it got there by turning the offense over to LaNorris Sellers and the run game. The Gamecocks opened the season with a 57-0 rout of Kent State, then hit a rough stretch with losses to Mississippi State , Alabama, and Kentucky , with the Alabama game their only SEC loss by more than one score. Since then, they've won back-to-back games over ranked opponents. On October 10, they rolled No. 16 Florida 38-19, with Sellers accounting for five touchdowns, four through the air and one on the ground, and last Saturday they beat No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 on a walk-off 48-yard field goal. Sellers had three touchdowns in that one, throwing for 210 yards and carrying 18 times for 96 yards, and the Gamecocks came out of the gate fast, going 75 yards in 10 plays on their opening drive and then scoring again on a 31-yard Sellers run to take a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. The strength of this team is its ground game, which leads the SEC at 218.3 yards a game. Sellers has 507 rushing yards at 6.0 a carry and Matt Fuller has 513 yards and five touchdowns, so defenses are forced to account for two backfield threats before Sellers throws a pass. The weak spots are in the trenches and on defense. The offensive line has allowed 15 sacks and is missing Josiah Thompson, Dayne Arnett and Seth Smith, receiver Jayden Sellers is also done for the season, and edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah is out. Defensive back Quay'sheed Scott and running back Jawarn Howell are doubtful. The defense ranks 119th in success rate , allows 222.7 passing yards a game, and has just four interceptions, which is why South Carolina's games tend to be decided by whether the offense keeps scoring. One key note: Shane Beamer, who was an assistant head coach for the offense at Oklahoma under Lincoln Riley, knows this program well. Oklahoma has been a defense-first team that is still looking for a consistent offense. The Sooners opened with a 51-0 win over UTEP , then lost to Michigan, beat New Mexico, and fell to Georgia before pulling off the season's biggest upset, a 27-24 win over then-No. 1 Texas on October 10 in the Red River Rivalry. They followed that with a 21-13 loss to No. 15 Kentucky at home, a game they led 13-7 into the fourth quarter before Mateer threw two interceptions, one returned for a touchdown, and last Saturday they beat Mississippi State 23-15 on the road. That win was their best offensive day of the season, 467 total yards, with John Mateer completing 22 of 29 passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns without a turnover and Isaiah Sategna catching eight passes for 164 yards, along with 184 rushing yards, well above their season average of 92.5. The identity is still their defense. Oklahoma ranks second in the SEC in total yards allowed and first in pass defense, with 22 sacks, and it ranks second in adjusted EPA per play and success rate. The offense is the problem. The Sooners rank last in the SEC in total offense, have the conference's worst run game and sit 121st in offensive success rate, and they've scored fewer than 30 points in six straight games, every SEC game this season included. Mateer has 1,591 passing yards, a 66.7% completion rate, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions, and Sategna leads the receivers with 578 yards. Lastly, the injury list is long, with linebacker Taylor Heim, receiver Trell Harris, tight end Trynae Washington, cornerback Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Eddy Pierre-Louis and Ryan Fodje out; receiver Elijah Thomas doubtful; and Peyton and Eli Bowen and linemen Jake Maikkula and Fred Hinton questionable. The case for South Carolina in the first quarter starts with the price. At +106, the market is treating the first 15 minutes as close to a coin flip, while the full-game line has Oklahoma as a 4.5- to 5.5-point favorite and South Carolina's moneyline anywhere from about +150 to +175. That gap makes sense, because Oklahoma's advantages are the kind that build over four quarters: a defense that ranks near the top of the SEC and can grind an opponent down over four quarters. However, those advantages don't help much early in a game, and the early part of the game is exactly where South Carolina's offense has been at its best. The gap between the two offenses is the other piece. South Carolina has the SEC's top rushing attack, Oklahoma has the conference's worst run game and 121st-ranked success rate, and the Sooners have not been quick starters in their recent games. They trailed Kentucky 7-0 after the first quarter, and against Mississippi State their entire first-quarter output was a field goal. South Carolina, meanwhile, scored on both of its first two possessions against Tennessee and has a quarterback who can make a defense pay with one big play, as he did on the 31-yard run. Oklahoma's defense is excellent, but a Sellers-Fuller running game that forces it to defend the whole field is the kind of look that can produce a scripted score, and winning the quarter may only take one good drive. The weather may also tilt things toward the visitors. The forecast calls for rain on Saturday, most likely before kickoff, with a high near 65, and a damp field tends to favor the team that wants to run the ball. The Gamecocks also fell behind early in the Florida game before taking over, so a slow start is possible, but with a +106 price for what is likely a much closer first quarter than the full-game odds suggest, South Carolina is the better side. picks.headline: Staff Picks: Can Oklahoma Build on Last Week's Success Against South Carolina?
picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Can Oklahoma Build on Last Week's Success Against South Carolina? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Canelo vs. Mbilli live updates NBA Cup: Friday roundup Steph breaks Luka's ankles NFL injury tracker Belichick-Hudson breakup Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer scans the defense before a snap against MSU. | Carson Field / Sooners On SI Ryan Chapman Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's going to be much harder to run the football this week against a stout South Carolina defense. If the Sooners can continue their upward trajectory against the Gamecocks, they'll have a chance. If not - if John Mateer has to lead the team in rushing attempts and the Sooners average less than 4 yards per carry, then desperation will set in, Mateer will be forced to make plays - then bad things will happen. But if OU can run the ball just a little, Mateer can relax and guys like Isaiah Sategna and Rocky Beers and Lloyd Avant can help out the defense by moving the chains, changing the scoreboard and winning a home game. Final: Oklahoma 21, South Carolina 13 John Mateer found a healthy headspace in Starkville, but Saturday will be the first real test to see if he can stick to the plan. South Carolina's defense is not impenetrable, but it's a much better group than Mississippi State's, with difference-makers who can wreck drives and put Mateer into tough situations. It's likely there will be a turnover, and the test will be if OU's quarterback can rebound after that. History says he'll have a tough time. Brent Venables' defense will get its third look at talented quarterback LaNorris Sellers, but if Oklahoma is unable to finish off drives, the Gamecocks have shown they can notch dramatic victories. Final: South Carolina 20, Oklahoma 13 Someone from the future could tell me a plethora of different outcomes from Saturday's game, and I'd believe them. Oklahoma's offense certainly made progress against Mississippi State, and it's possible that the Sooners build on those improvements at home against South Carolina. But it also wouldn't be shocking if OU's offense regressed into the turnover-prone unit that it was against Kentucky, Georgia, New Mexico and Michigan. South Carolina comes into Norman on a two-game winning streak after ranked victories over Florida (on the road) and Tennessee - the Gamecocks seem like they're due for a letdown. While South Carolina's defense is better than Mississippi State's was, there are plenty of areas for the Sooners to expose, assuming they can play a similarly clean game on Saturday. Oklahoma needs a win to stay above .500, and I expect the Sooners to earn a close victory over the Gamecocks. Final: Oklahoma 20, South Carolina 17 The Gamecocks are more dangerous than Mississippi State, on both sides of the ball. Last week was a small step forward for the Sooners' offense, nota giant leap. Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't completely fixed just because he had a solid game against the Bulldogs. But with Michael Fasusi back on the offensive line, the Sooners' offense adds layers. They don't have to have every element working in order to be successful. What they do need to do, though, is protect the football and keep up their strong defensive play. This game will be back and forth and figures to go down to the wire, but in the end, Oklahoma does just enough to start its first winning streak of the season. Brady Trantham The 2026 season is still up in the air. One thing it has told us is that basically no one has been able to handle a big emotional win and follow that up with another win a week later. South Carolina's win over Tennessee was very much an emotional win against a highly-ranked opponent - the Volunteers themselves had just beaten Alabama the week prior. OU has slowly built consistency on offense, just enough that paired with an elite defense, victories against flawed teams are realistic. The Sooners have proven to be great at corralling mobile quarterbacks and will showcase that again, while John Mateer will build off a great performance last week against a dangerous but very gettable defense. (Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Michael Sauls Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads South Carolina football is hitting the road this weekend. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will travel to Norman, Oklahoma, on Saturday to face Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 4:15 and will be televised on SEC Network. South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) is coming off a big win over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week. Oklahoma beat Mississippi State last week on the road. The Gamecocks and Sooners have played just twice in the all-time series. South Carolina beat Oklahoma on the road in 2024 and the Sooners beat the Gamecocks last year in Columbia. Here's what you need to know about Saturday's game: Is South Carolina vs. Oklahoma football game on TV? Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay'sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you're making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren't expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather's 10-day forecast. There's a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three's a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven't won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks' SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven't looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That's certainly good, but USC's running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn't on Sellers' legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina's savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn't necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC's kicking competition this offseason. But he's quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller's absence because of injury. Hay's Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer's name this offseason, but he's found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He's got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer's favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards.

Can a South Carolina team with three SEC losses get to the College Football Playoff? If it closes with seven straight wins – including last week's victory over Tennessee and a win in late November against Georgia – it's not totally off the table. Can an Oklahoma team with three losses get to the College Football Playoff? If it closes with five straight wins – including the win over Texas a few weeks ago and if it picks up November wins over Florida, Ole Miss, and Missouri – it's not totally off the table. But the loser of this is definitely out – the CFP won't take a four-loss at-large team. The winner survives, advances, and can keep the dream alive. South Carolina vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes to Florida next, but this starts a run of three of the next four games at home. South Carolina hosts Texas A&M next before going to Arkansas. It closes with Georgia and at Clemson. It's only the third meeting between the two. Oklahoma won 26-7 last year, but South Carolina won 35-9 in 2024. How To Watch South Carolina vs Oklahoma Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 4:15 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Memorial Stadium, Norman, OK – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why South Carolina Will Win South Carolina is playing like a team that's having fun. It's not like it's going out there with no more fudge (this is a family show) to give after losing three straight, but it's been loose, relatively relaxed, and it's balling out with strong wins over Florida and Tennessee. The turnovers slowed to a crawl after giving it away twice in four straight games – there was just one interception against Tennessee in the last two – and the defense has done its part with three takeaways against Florida and one against the Vols. Why Oklahoma Will Win Oklahoma is still cranking up the defense, but it's just about the scoring. Sometimes the Sooners have to manufacture points from other areas – like they did against Texas – and that's where the defense has to come up large. The D doesn't have to score, but it needs to force South Carolina to start screwing up again. Oklahoma has come up with takeaways four times, with two in each game. It's 3-1 when it forces mistakes, because that leads to easy points for a team that's struggling to get the offense consistently moving. South Carolina vs Oklahoma Prediction, Betting Lines Okay, which flaky way do you want to do this? Oklahoma is 4-0 when scoring at least 14 points, and 0-3 when it scores fewer. South Carolina has only allowed fewer than 19 points twice, and that was against Kent State and Towson. However, the Gamecocks are 4-0 when allowing fewer than 35 points. You want to get even sillier? Okay, let's go. In a never-screw-with-a-streak sort of way, Oklahoma has alternated win-loss-win-loss from the start, and if the pattern holds, it's due for a loss. To rein this in, South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers is playing well at just the right time. He might not be going crazy, but he's making plays, keeping things moving, and he's playing like a quarterback who can win games. The four-touchdown pass win at Florida showed what he could do on the road. In this, he'll have to make one or two big plays late. As he showed against Tennessee, he can do that. The National Council on Problem Gambling help line is also often cited at 1-800-522-4700. Broadcast Details - TV: SEC Network and ESPN Unlimited (Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik and Michella Chester) - Radio: Sooner Sports Network via 107.7 The Franchise/KOKC 95.3 and 1520 in Oklahoma City, 1430 The Buzz/KMOD 97.5 in Tulsa, and on The Varsity Network app (Toby Rowland, Teddy Lehman, Chris Plank, and Gabe Ikard) What You Need To Know NORMAN, Okla. — Oklahoma's season has refused to settle into anything comfortable. Saturday's homecoming game against South Carolina is the next chance to stop the bouncing. The Sooners are 4-3 and 2-2 in the SEC heading into a 3:15 p.m. kickoff at Gaylord Family — Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. South Carolina arrives at 4-3 and 2-3, receiving votes, and playing with the confidence of a team that just knocked off Florida and Tennessee. That alone should wipe out any idea that this is a soft home date. The Gamecocks have already shown they can travel, finish close games, and lean on a quarterback who creates problems Oklahoma has to solve with discipline more than highlight-hunt pressure. There is history all over this one too. Shane Beamer spent 2018 through 2020 in Norman as Oklahoma's assistant head coach on offense, working tight ends and H-backs during a 33-6 stretch that included three Big 12 titles and two College Football Playoff appearances. Brent Venables, meanwhile, spent years tormenting South Carolina from the Clemson sideline. He went 7-2 against the Gamecocks as defensive coordinator and held them to 14.9 points per game in those seven wins. The recent series between these two programs has swung hard both ways: South Carolina won 35-9 in Norman in 2024 after Oklahoma turned it over on its first three possessions, then the Sooners answered with a 26-7 road win last year by smothering the Gamecocks and winning the line of scrimmage. That 2024 home loss is still the warning label. Oklahoma actually outgained South Carolina that day and held them to 69 second-half yards. It did not matter. Four turnovers and a 24-0 deficit in points off turnovers decided the afternoon before the Sooners ever found their footing. That has been the split-screen identity of this entire season too. In the wins over Texas and Mississippi State, Oklahoma had four takeaways and only one giveaway. In the losses to Georgia and Kentucky, it had two takeaways and eight giveaways. When the Sooners protect the ball, they look like a team that can still climb. When they do not, the defense gets asked to cover for a mess it did not create. The weirdest layer is the pattern. Oklahoma has followed every win with a loss and every loss with a win through seven games, the first time in program history the Sooners have alternated results across the first seven contests. If that pattern holds, homecoming would be a loss. That is exactly the kind of empty narrative this team needs to bury. South Carolina is the seventh straight opponent that was ranked or receiving votes at kickoff. The schedule has not given Oklahoma many clean emotional resets. This is another one that will have heat on it from the start. Oklahoma's defense remains the reason this team is still interesting. The Sooners lead the nation in first downs allowed per game and sit among the national leaders in third-down defense, red-zone defense, pass defense, sacks, and total defense. Opponents have scored on just 23 percent of their possessions. All 14 defensive starters began their college careers at Oklahoma. Owen Heinecke continues to lead the team in tackles and has become the week-to-week constant at linebacker. The front still has enough disruption to wreck drives when the edges stay clean. South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers is built to test that cleanliness. He is a big, physical quarterback who can push the ball downfield and punish soft contain with his legs. He has already thrown for more than 1,500 yards and added over 500 on the ground. The Gamecocks' recent upswing has come with far better ball security and enough confidence to finish against ranked teams. If Oklahoma's edge players get greedy or abandon lanes, Sellers can turn ordinary scrambles into drive-extending runs. The Sooners need a cage-rush approach more than a free-for-all. Squeeze the pocket, stay in assignment, and make him beat the structure with processing instead of freelancing into open space. Peyton Bowen's status adds some stress on the back end. He has been one of Oklahoma's most important defensive players all season, with takeaways that directly turned into points against Texas and Mississippi State. He is also coming out of the Mississippi State game dealing with a leg/stinger issue. If he is limited, somebody else has to clean up the explosive answers and help finish when Sellers extends plays. South Carolina's best chance is not a perfect 12-play drive script. It is one broken containment snap and one missed tackle in space. John Mateer's Starkville tape is the first real reset of the year at quarterback. He completed 22 of 29 passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns, did not throw an interception, and helped Oklahoma post season highs in total offense and rushing in a road win. Isaiah Sategna went off for 164 yards. Rocky Beers stayed productive. The run game finally had some weight to it, including a long run from Tory Blaylock that flipped the third quarter. Venables has already said that version of Mateer is what Oklahoma needs the rest of the way. That has to show up again Saturday. Mateer is at 1,591 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and seven interceptions on the season. The efficiency can play. The turnover number is still the ceiling-cutter. South Carolina will give him enough looks to get comfortable if he stays patient and uses Beers as the safety valve while Sategna works the intermediate and deep parts of the field. Beers has been one of the better transfer additions in the league and continues to lead SEC tight ends in receiving yards per game. Sategna remains the explosive piece defenses have to account for every series. The offensive line remains the quieter concern. Availability has been uneven all season, and Oklahoma has had to patch together combinations on the fly. Against a South Carolina front that will try to clutter lanes and force Mateer into longer holds, that matters. The Sooners do not need 500 yards again. They need manageable downs, fewer empty possessions, and enough balance to keep Sellers' offense from owning the tempo of the day. There is a temptation to overstate every remaining game because the margin is already thin. Fair enough. ESPN's FPI has Oklahoma projected around the 6-6 range, and the remaining stretch still includes Florida, Ole Miss, Texas A&M, and Missouri. That means Saturday is not just another home date. It is one of the clearer opportunities to create breathing room. A win over South Carolina would make Oklahoma 5-3 and 3-2, with some actual traction in league play. It would also reinforce the only formula that has worked this year: defense travels, takeaways matter, and the quarterback has to stop donating points. A loss would push the Sooners back into the same uneasy place they occupied after Kentucky, with the season again asking whether the good nights are sustainable or just occasional interruptions. South Carolina is not an unknown. Beamer knows Norman. Sellers can take over a game if Oklahoma gets careless. The Gamecocks are playing better now than they were in September. All of that is true. It is also true that Oklahoma can win this game if it plays like the team that handled Texas and Mississippi State instead of the one that buried itself in turnovers against Georgia and Kentucky. Homecoming should not require a miracle. It requires cleanliness. Keep Sellers crowded. Make South Carolina drive the hard way. Let Mateer play the next snap instead of the last mistake. If the Sooners do that, Norman should still be a hard place to leave with a win. If they do not, the pattern everyone is already talking about will get one more chapter.

away.blurb: For the Gamecocks, defensive back Quay’sheed Scott was ruled out in Friday’s availability report. Scott has nine tackles this season, including one for loss. Offensive lineman Carter Miller, who has missed the last two games for South Carolina, is no longer on the report and is available. Running back Jawarn Howell has been ruled out. The Southeastern Conference has released its final availability report for No. 11 Tennessee’s game at South Carolina . For the Vols, no players have been added to the report other than the six who were lost for the season earlier this year: Tennessee will head into the game as an underdog despite its No. 11 national ranking. Head coach Josh Heupel preached fundamentals and preparation this week. “I’ve said it to our football team, I think I’ve said it here a couple times, every week’s a new season inside of this league. That’s whether you’re playing at home or on the road, you’ve got to play,” Heupel said Monday. “The margins are just, they’re small, they’re tight. A play here, a call there, can make a huge difference. So, you’ve got to be on the right side of it in your preparation.” Below is the full South Carolina availability report: No. 11 Tennessee and South Carolina are set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Williams-Brice Stadium. away.blurb: On offense, key players Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis aren't close to returning and were ruled out. However, guard Heath Ozaeta could make his first appearance since the win over Texas. Ozaeta was listed as probable. If he's able to play, he provides Oklahoma a valuable piece to its interior offensive line rotation. If he's able to play, it's likely Ozaeta slides back into the starting lineup, though he could platoon with Peyton Joseph, who has had ups and downs for the Sooners the last two weeks. It also looks like running back Xavier Robinson could be available this week. The Carl Albert High School graduate hasn't played since the Week 4 loss to Georgia and played fewer than 10 snaps in back-to-back weeks before suffering a calf strain. He'll battle with Jonathan Hatton for the third running back carries as Lloyd Avant and Tory Blaylock have established themselves as the Sooners' 1-2 punch in the running back rotation. Defensively, the Oklahoma Sooners have big questions. Rotation linebacker Cole Sullivan was ruled out for this week. Safety Peyton Bowen and cornerback Eli Bowen are both questionable for Week 9. Both Bowens are key pieces to the Sooners' defense, and against a good South Carolina passing attack, Peyton Bowen's presence is critical. He's one of the best safeties in college football. If he can't play, it'll be Omarion Robinson and Michael Boganowski starting at the safety spots, and potentially Reggie Powers mixing into the rotation. If Eli Bowen is out, Trystan Haynes would likely get another start. He's been solid since entering the starting lineup against the Texas Longhorns and would need to be at his best this week if called upon to start. Injuries have once again been a key storyline for the Sooners in the 2026 season. If the key players listed as questionable and probable can be available for this week, it would give the Sooners a boost on both sides of the football. home.blurb: Mississippi State's offense looked out of sorts last week against LSU without Kamario Taylor, as the Bulldogs' offense was shut out for the first time in six seasons. Initial signs from Wednesday's SEC player availability report signaled ... maybe. Taylor remained listed as questionable for the Bulldogs' SEC matchup against the Sooners, according to Friday's player availability report. as he continues to recover from an undisclosed injury. Pete Thamel reported on Oct. 24 , however, Taylor will in fact be playing through his malady against the Sooners. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. Oklahoma. He remained questionable on Friday, but according to Pete Thamel, he will play against Oklahoma. Taylor was downgraded to out ahead of last Saturday's game against LSU due to an undisclosed injury. Before kickoff, he was seen wearing street clothes and a walking boot on the sideline. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. Lebby noted in his postgame news conference after the 56-23 loss to Alabama that Taylor had been dealing with a prior injury heading into the game. What injury does Kamario Taylor have? Taylor is dealing with an undisclosed lower-body injury. Ryan Minion Sat, October 31, 2026 at 10:42 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Clemson Tigers take on the Florida State Seminoles in Tallahassee, Florida, on Saturday, Oct. 31. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. ET on the ACC Network. Florida State is favored by -6.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -210. Clemson, meanwhile, enters as a +6.5 underdog and is +172 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 50.5 total points. Here's my Clemson vs. Florida State prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 31. Clemson vs. Florida State Pick: Florida State ML My Florida State vs. Clemson best bet is on the Seminoles to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Clemson vs Florida State Odds Clemson vs Florida State point spread : Florida State -6.5 (-102), Clemson +6.5 (-120) Clemson vs Florida State over/under : 50.5 (-106o / -114u) Clemson vs Florida State moneyline : Clemson +172, Florida State -210 It has been a rocky first seven games for the Tigers. Freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds has struggled mightily in his first collegiate season, throwing just one passing touchdown throughout the Tigers' first seven contests. Reynolds has been far from efficient as well, tossing three interceptions with a 32.8 QBR that ranks outside the top 120 nationally. Head coach Dabo Swinney's offense is extremely one-dimensional, relying heavily on sophomore tailback Gideon Davidson, who's not having a great campaign either. Davidson has rushed for 492 yards with five rushing touchdowns on 93 carries. Still, not particularly impressive either when you compare Davidson's stats on a national scale. This offense is completely lost out there and now must travel into a very challenging conference showdown in Tallahassee. On the defensive side of the ball, Clemson has been far better, allowing its opponents just over 21 points per game over the first seven contests of the season. The 'Noles offense will be a very tough challenge for Clemson's defense, especially after they nearly upset top-ranked Miami on the road just two weeks ago. Despite Clemson's struggles, it's actually Florida State that has the worse regular-season record despite opening as a 6-point favorite this week. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has been quite impressive over his first seven games as a Seminole after transferring from Auburn via the portal. Daniels ranks inside the top 40 among quarterbacks with 1,618 passing yards and 12 touchdown passes on the season. However, turnovers have been a problem for him, throwing eight interceptions. That said, Daniels still boasts an extremely impressive 81.9 QBR, ranking 16th among all quarterbacks. A great deal of Daniels' success has resulted from the sizable contributions made by star wide receiver Duce Robinson, who has racked up over 400 receiving yards and four touchdowns. FSU's rushing attack was quite stable until it wasn't. Sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah was in the midst of a breakout season until a broken ankle knocked him out for the remainder of the season. With Kromah's absence, it falls on the back of Texas transfer Quintrevion Wisner, who has been effective as well, rushing for over 200 yards on just 38 carries this season. Wisner does have experience as a bell-cow, though, running for over 1,000 yards in his second year with the Longhorns. Florida State has been far more vulnerable defensively, allowing its first seven opponents of the season nearly 28 points per game (27.9). Fortunately for FSU, the 'Noles defense has a prime bounce-back opportunity on Saturday night given how poorly Reynolds has played. We're in for a great one on Saturday night in a prime-time spot featuring two rivals. While some may be surprised by the Seminoles' standing as a six-point favorite over a Clemson bunch with a superior record, I disagree and expect the prime-time slot to give Florida State a considerable edge playing in front of a packed home crowd. Despite the 'Noles sub-.500 record and the fact they're currently on a two-game skid, I was very impressed with the way head coach Mike Norvell's offense looked against Miami. Though Florida State's defense is undoubtedly weak, Reynolds has looked awful, and this matchup looks like such a prime bounce-back spot for the Seminoles. While I'm not crazy about laying 6 points on Florida State, I'm confident they win the game outright, so I'm electing to wager on Seminoles moneyline at -210. Pick: Florida State ML (-210)

picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Clemson Tigers | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 31, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looks to get to .500 and avoid 3rd straight loss as home favorites The Florida State Seminoles will host the Clemson Tigers this Saturday for a Halloween evening rivalry game at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. The kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and the game will be televised by the ACCN. This will be the 39th meeting between the teams, with Florida State (3-4, 1-3 ACC) leading the all-time series 21-17, including a 12-7 record at Doak and an 18-15 record as ACC members. However, Clemson has won the last two meetings and holds a 15-7 advantage over the last 22 games, including wins in nine of the last 10 meetings. Clemson will be attempting to win a fifth consecutive game at Doak, becoming only the third program ever to win five consecutive road games against FSU in Tallahassee, joining Florida (six straight from 1966-76) and Miami (Fla.) (five from 1957-77). Despite Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State combining for 13 of the last 15 ACC championships, both teams are struggling this year. Clemson’s losses have come against #15 LSU, #1 Miami, and a 6-2 Virginia Tech team that scored the winning touchdown with 1:44 left on the clock. FSU’s four losses were in double overtime at #1 Miami, at #10 Alabama, at home against #19 SMU, and at Louisville when the defense totally collapsed. Clemson’s defense is the strength of their team. The Tigers rank 32nd in total defense (317), 36th in passing (186), T-53rd in rushing defense (131), T-30th in third-down defense (holding opponents to a 33.3-percent conversion rate), have allowed only four passing touchdowns, and have recorded 20 sacks through seven games. The Tigers’ passing offense, behind true freshman QB Tait Reynolds, who was named starter following an injury to Christopher Vizzina in their 2nd game, has only thrown one touchdown, and the 2 QBs combined have only thrown 2 TDs all season. Reynolds has been sacked 20 times this season and has thrown 3 interceptions while averaging just 6.1 yards per completion. Overall, Clemson has allowed 21 sacks, rank 115th in total offense (333). 112th in scoring offense, 115th in passing offense, 126th in 3rd-down conversion (31.7%), and 93rd in red zone offense. Florida State looks to avoid its 3rd straight loss after a heartbreaking double-overtime loss to Miami. The Noles were able to rush for 138 yards against the nation’s #1-ranked rushing defense; however, leading rusher Ousmane Kromah sustained a lower-leg injury and will miss the rest of the 2026 season. FSU loses double-overtime heartbreaker to Miami Social media reactions to the end of FSU vs. Miami Column: ACC replay review never entertained another outcome on FSU’s final play FSU running back Ousmane Kromah carted off near the end of first half against Miami Despite having a losing season record, FSU’s offense is ranked T-49th in the nation in total offense, 50th in scoring, 46th in rushing, 63rd in passing, and 34th in red-zone offense. FSU individual leaders After allowing Miami to rack up 583 total yards on 78 plays for a 7.5 yard average/play, FSU’s defense now ranks 130th in the nation, giving up 435 yards/game, 124th in passing defense (256 yards/game), T-112th in third-down percentage, allowing opponents to convert nearly 43% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-104th in first-down defense, allowing their opponents 155 first downs (22.1/game) in the 7 games played this season. Florida State is currently trending as a 5.5-point favorite with the over/under set at 49.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Clemson Tigers Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Jordan Silversmith (season record: 6-1) This game is a tricky one to call. I do not think Clemson is a good football team. However, they probably have the best unit on the field: their defense. Another issue for Florida State is that the Seminoles have historically struggled against the Tigers, with no home wins in the last decade. Even so, FSU should win on Saturday night. I imagine that, off a bye, head coach Mike Norvell will scheme up points on the opening drive, and Tony White’s defense should make forcing CU to throw the name of the game. This game will be close, as it often is with FSU, but Clemson isn’t good enough right now to win a rivalry game on the road. Seminole win, but no cover. FSU 27, Clemson 24 Tim Scribble (season record: 6-1) This could be a scary game, fitting for Halloween. With Kromah out, Clemson’s defense may keep FSU in check but the Tiger’s offense is dreadful. If Clemson somehow overwhelm’s Tony White’s defense, that relationship needs to end. I think FSU wins but it will be ugly. FSU 24, Clemson 17 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) Call me crazy, but this game is going to be completely unwatchable but FSU will emerge victorious. Firstly, it’s at Doak. On Halloween. Where else would you rather be? In all seriousness, Clemson’s offensive efficiency is dreadful. Like, REALLY dreadful. Per Game On Paper , Clemson’s EPA per pass is #136 out of #138 and their EPA per rush is #110. They are only 33.7% successful on third down, good for #128, and they are just bad at most things offense, mainly because their QB is a freshman. Their defense is good to great, though! #13 in EPA/Pass defense and just middle of the pack on rushing defense, #64 in the nation. Florida State meanwhile… their defense is trash. #127 on EPA per pass, #105 on EPA per rush, #120 on 3rd/4th down stops. The offense is good, though. #39 in EPA/Pass, #36 in EPA/Rush. If they can handle Clemson’s terrible offense and do good things on defense against a very not good Clemson offense, it might be a fun halloweekend in Tallahassee. Give me the Noles to pull off, not an upset per se, just a good, scrappy win. Florida State 14, Clemson 13 Curt Weiler (season record: 5-2, 2-5 ATS) Call me crazy for buying in again but I think I believe in this FSU team more than I do that Clemson team. The Tigers’ defense is pretty good. But the offense is very bad. Clemson is the only FBS team which has scored more points from its defense/special teams than its offense . To Tony White and his unit, I would say “If not now, when?” FSU 27, Clemson 20 NoleThruandThru (season record: 7-0) I’m taking a break from the Marshawn gag this week to honor my dad, who passed away two weeks ago. The world lost a wonderful FSU alum and fan, and I hope he enjoys this one from heaven. FSU 28, Clemson 24 Jon Marchant (season record: 6-1 ) Nobody knows what kind of team FSU will be from week to week. No result is off the table and there’s no score that would surprise anyone. So I’m picking FSU this week. Just cause. Also, it’s funny when Dabo loses. Clemson 23, FSU 28 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 5-1) I’m picking FSU but I don’t feel great about the prediction. I’m really worried about what FSU’s offense will look like without Kromah vs. Clemson’s defense. That being said I have not seen enough from Clemson’s offense to stay off the field and if you give FSU’s skill group enough shots they’re going to get points. Noles win. FSU 24 Clemson 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 5-2; ATS: 4-3) As others have said, Clemson’s offense is putrid. Two passing touchdowns all season long is nearly unfathomable. But is Tony White’s defense just what the doctor ordered? It’s the moveable object vs the stoppable force. I’ve said all year that despite all the suckage over the last three seasons, FSU has honestly been pretty decent at home. However, Norvell’s teams also have a penchant for finding ways to lose very winnable games. If Kromah was healthy, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If Quindarious Jones was healthy I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. If a random FCS DC who’s name was drawn out of a hat was FSU’s defensive coordinator, I’d feel a lot better about the ‘Noles. Clemson 30 , FSU 28 Frank DNole (season record: 3-4) FSU’s offense is better than Clemson’s defense. Clemson’s offense is about as good as FSU’s defense. Advantage Noles. This will be the game that turns the program around, and everything comes together for the Noles. The Noles are 5.5-point favorites for a reason. Vegas knows something and the Seminoles know it too. The game will follow a similar storyline to what we witnessed against Virginia. The Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special teams battles because the FSU players will give 110% more effort, they will want it more, and they will play with more heart than their equally talented Clempsun opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, Orange Dabo’s 27 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 4-3, 3-4 ATS) For all its flaws over the last two seasons, FSU has taken care of business against the teams it should beat while in the confines of Doak. I have faith in FSU’s ability to get enough points against a stout Clemson defense and, as naive as it might be, take care of business against a dreadful Tigers offense. picks.blurb: Clemson Tigers final odds and prediction for Week 9 at Florida State Seminoles Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's basketball Women's basketball Baseball and softball FanSided NCAA Sites Clemson has been left with no choice but to pick up the pieces after last week's soul-crushing loss to Virginia Tech. It may have only counted as one defeat on the ledger, but it really did feel like 2.5 losses mentally. For better or worse, the Tigers must turn the page and get ready for potentially a wild road game at the rival Florida State Seminoles. It will be during Halloween, nevertheless, so get ready for it. Clemson enters play at 4-3 on the season and 2-2 in the ACC. It has wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, Cal, and Charleston Southern, with losses to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech. While Florida State is only 3-4 on the season, Mike Norvell's Seminoles have a knack for scoring points and playing some fairly competitive football at home. Dabo Swinney cannot let his team overlook FSU. With that all in mind, here are the latest betting odds, how to watch this game, and a game prediction. Latest betting odds for Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles According to the FanDuel Sportsbook , Florida State will be laying 5.5 points to visiting Clemson. The associated moneylines for this game are Florida State -215 and Clemson +180. This means that it would take a $215 bet on Florida State to win $100, while wagering $100 on Clemson would pocket you $180. The projected point total for the game comes in at a combined 49.5 points, down from 51.5. Using all of that information above, a projected final score for this game would be something in the vicinity of Florida State 27.5, Clemson 22. While the odds for this game have fluctuated a bit , Florida State has been the favorite throughout for two reasons. It is a home game for the Seminoles, and the meager Tigers' offense has struggled to score points against Power Four competition all season long. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. How to watch Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles Here is what you need to know to be able to watch Clemson take on Florida State on Halloween night. Date: Saturday, Oct. 31 Time: 7:00 p.m. ET Location: Tallahassee, FL Venue: Doak Campbell Stadium TV Info: ACCN Streaming Info: fuboTV Radio: 105.5 FM (The Roar)/Clemson Athletic Network Kickoff from Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee, FL, will be at 7:00 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 31. The ACC Network will carry the conference rivalry game. You can stream the game on fuboTV. You can listen to the game over the airwaves on 105.5 FM The Roar, or you can check out any other radio affiliates on the Clemson Athletic Network. You are not going to want to miss this rivalry game! Clemson Tigers at Florida State Seminoles game prediction This high-stakes ACC rivalry game will come down to one of two things. From the Florida State perspective, it will be all about how disciplined the Seminoles' pass defense will be. This team can score points, but it does love to give them up in bunches. As for Clemson, the Tigers need to show on offense that they can put up 30 or so points if they need to get into some sort of a low-end shootout. Right now, it is so hard to fathom Clemson getting into the end zone at least three times on Saturday. The Tigers are going to need three touchdowns, and presumably 12 points from Nolan Hauser on special teams, to realistically have a chance at pulling off the upset. Gideon Davidson may get one on the ground, possibly two if he gets lucky. This will come down to whether Tait Reynolds can throw for one. Unfortunately, Clemson's offense is not built right now to score quickly and in bunches, so it will lose. Week 9 final score prediction: Florida State 30, Clemson 24. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, doesn't favor the Tigers, either. It gives Florida State a 71.9% chance to win and Clemson a 28.1% chance. The Tigers are 51st nationally in ESPN's FPI with a 5.8 rating, which ranks 11th among the 17 ACC teams. Florida State has a 10.1 FPI rating that's 37th nationally. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Kansas State (5.7) and one spot below Virginia (6.0). Clemson football odds of reaching bowl game after brutal Week 7 loss to Virginia Tech In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 78.1%, down from 88.4% prior to its loss to Virginia Tech. Clemson's chances of winning its final five games are just 2.1%, according to ESPN's FPI. ESPN explains: "The Football Power Index (FPI) is a measure of team strength that is meant to be the best predictor of a team's performance going forward for the rest of the season. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." Clemson football vs. Florida State start time, TV channel information Kickoff for Clemson-Florida State in Week 9 of the 2026 college football season is 7 p.m. ET Saturday at Doak Campbell Stadium in Tallahassee. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. home.headline: Quindarrius Jones injury update: Florida State's banged-up secondary continues to take hits
home.blurb: With the game against Clemson quickly approaching for Florida State, a top defensive back has been ruled out. Starting corner Quindarrius Jones left the game against Miami in Week 7 after playing just 14 snaps. Jones had a week to recover with the bye, which brought some hope, but the defender will not be able to play against Clemson. Jones has missed two games this season now after sitting out the home game against Central Arkansas earlier in the year. Frankly, it was better for the defense to play Central Arkansas without him, so more defensive backs would be able to see the field. However, against Clemson, Florida State cannot afford to suffer another injury at an already weak position. The secondary has been torn to shreds all year, with Karson Hobbs and Jamari Howard spending the majority of the season on the injury report. Jones has missed time, freshman Jordan Crutchfield has been unavailable most of the season, and Chuck Kennon was dismissed just as he began to recover from an injury. With Jones out, two players will likely take over: Charles Lester III and Jordan Crutchfield, who will be making his return from an injury against Clemson. Lester has been the main replacement for Jones this season, playing 33 snaps against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester also replaced Jones for the game against Central Arkansas, logging 34 snaps. Jones typically plays between 45 and 55 snaps each week, with his total number of snaps played increasing as the injuries in the secondary have stacked up. Lester has been covering a good portion of the missing snaps, but against Miami, Ja'Bril Rawls played 74 out of 80 possible snaps, which is something he has done multiple times this season. Lester is more than likely going to resume the same role he has previously taken when Jones is forced to sit out, but the addition of a healthy Crutchfield gives the staff options. Fellow safety KJ Kirkland is expected to play, but has been dealing with an injury, which could create a different avenue to the field for Crutchfield. In limited playing time this season, Lester has proven to be effective at times, with eight total tackles, including three against Miami after Jones left the game. Lester has struggled at times in coverage, but his ability to recover and limit additional gains is notable. Starters have to play virtually the entire game to compensate for the fact that there is no depth, and the result has been a tired defense that often falls apart late in games. Jones missing the game against Clemson certainly hurts, but the Seminoles have been in this position multiple times already this season, and a plan is likely already in place. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Miami looks to stay unbeaten against a sneaky-good North Carolina team on the road Getty Images Prior to last week, Miami had not held the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 poll since 2002, but so far the Hurricanes are looking every bit the part of the best team in the country. Not only have they raced out to a 7-0 start this year, but they've done so in a way that suggests a continuation of the success that led Miami all the way to the national championship game last season. With a 14-1 record in its last 15 games, Miami has been one of the best teams in the country since early November 2025, and now each week provides yet another opportunity for this year's team to validate that high poll ranking. This week, that means a trip to Chapel Hill to take on Bill Belichick and North Carolina in a game that offers Cristobal and Miami a chance to reverse a recent skid in the series. The Tar Heels have won their last five meetings in the series, including a 2-0 record against Cristobal with wins in 2022 and 2023. But those two Miami teams finished a combined 12-13 overall, while this year's group is clearly playing on a different level. For starters, those teams didn't have not just one but two Heisman Trophy contenders like Miami does this year with quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney . Those last teams that lost to North Carolina also didn't carry the nation's best scoring margin, as Miami does currently, beating opponents by 33.7 points per game. There's some history that favors UNC, sure, but Miami's strength will challenge the impact of the past. Miami vs. North Carolina: Need to know Tar Heels looking to bounce back from upset home loss: While Miami validated its position at No. 1 last week with a thorough thrashing of Pitt, North Carolina saw some of the hype for this matchup cooled by an upset loss at home to Syracuse . The Tar Heels led by 10 points in the fourth quarter but let Steve Angeli and the Orange offense back into the game with a couple late scores before eventually falling in overtime. That's brought even more urgency to Bill Belichick's crew to have their game locked in for Saturday night, because the kind of failure at the margins that led to the fourth-quarter collapse will only be exposed more dramatically against a team of Miami's caliber. The Tar Heels have shown in wins over TCU , Pitt and Duke that they can play a tight game and come out on the right side of close margins, but those victories (and certainly any upset effort against Miami) require a cleaner effort than North Carolina showed against Syracuse last week. A Saturday showcase spot for Miami's Heisman Trophy contenders: Miami has a nice two-week run where its opponents and the stage will allow for quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney to receive a big-time spotlight in the national conversation. This week's game against North Carolina, on Halloween night in Chapel Hill, will draw plenty of attention and could allow the Hurricanes (who are 14-point favorites) to continue building the resumes of both Mensah and Toney. Mensah is putting together one of the best starts to a season we have seen from a quarterback this century, currently leading the nation in completion percentage (81.4%) while also rolling up 22 passing touchdowns (2nd in FBS) and 307.3 passing yards per game (fourth in FBS). Malachi Toney, meanwhile, leads the FBS in receptions (66) and has become the first wide receiver with at least 900 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns on a 7-0 team since eventual Heisman winner DeVonta Smith in 2020. Miami is elite in the middle (of games): It's easy to look at the collection of talent Mario Cristobal has assembled as an explanation for the team's dominance, but that talent has to perform to deliver the kind of results the Hurricanes have been getting over the last two seasons. Part of winning big has been winning small, and for Miami that's included dominating the middle portions of games. The Hurricanes have the No. 1 point differential in the second quarter in all of FBS (+95) and No. 3 point differential in the third quarter (+57). Miami is also No. 3 nationally this season in "middle 8" scoring (the last four minutes of the second quarter and the first four minutes of the third quarter), with a +7.6-point average on the season. The Hurricanes, ranked No. 4 at the time, were 6-0 and looking to establish themselves as the class of the ACC, having joined the conference just a few years removed from a national championship. A lot has been made about Miami's struggles in the last five meetings, but the Hurricanes' issues with the Heels date back to the very beginning of their time in the league, and Connor Barth's game-winning kick to seal the spooky upset. Bill Belichick and North Carolina's defense can get enough stops to keep this close, and with Notre Dame on deck, the Hurricanes might not be in the mindset to push this game deep into the evening. We're projecting North Carolina to flirt with the cover, but ultimately for the total to come in under the oddsmaker's number. away.headline: Notre Dame can survive its latest injury wave against Navy, but Miami is different
away.blurb: Notre Dame football’s “ next man up ” philosophy should be enough to get Marcus Freeman through Navy despite another crowded injury report. But with DJ McKinney out, Brauntae Johnson still sidelined, and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa among the questionable players, Chris Ash needs that list to shrink considerably before Miami arrives. Despite the Fighting Irish coming off a bye week , head coach Marcus Freeman detailed several injuries that will hit Chris Ash’s unit hard. The good news is that none of the players who will miss time or be questionable are ones the team should need against Navy. The question is how healthy some of these guys will be in two weeks against Miami. On Monday afternoon, Freeman said McKinney is out for the Navy game with an ankle injury. That’s never good news, as that kind of injury can stick around for a while. A cornerback who can’t make cuts won’t keep up with receivers. That’s not an issue against Navy, but against Miami, especially Malachi Toney, it’s a big one. Another big injury update: safety Brauntae Johnson is still out. Notre Dame has hoped he’d be out for “just a couple of weeks” after he was injured in the first half of the season opener. However, with the season now in Week 8, people have to start worrying about whether he will play this year. The injury list doesn’t end there. Freeman said that tight end Cooper Flanagan (hamstring), linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa (thumb), defensive lineman Loghan Thomas (shoulder), and cornerback Mark Zackery IV (concussion) are all questionable. Of course, of all the injuries that might just be cautionary, KVA’s questionable status is the most likely situation where he could have been fine to play if Miami was this week. Notre Dame should absolutely be able to beat Navy even without Viliamu-Asa in the lineup. The injury that should make Notre Dame faithful most worried is DJ McKinney’s. The transfer cornerback was hurt late in the game against BYU , and the bye week apparently wasn't enough time for him to heal and get back to 100%. Notre Dame football defensive injuries create bigger questions for Miami than Navy Because Notre Dame knows Navy won’t tax its cornerbacks much, sitting McKinney this week isn’t a shock. It’s even possible that if this were Miami week , they’d be working to get him back on the field. The Irish won’t push it against the Midshipmen. The most interesting note in that group is that Notre Dame took quite a bit of heat for not playing Viliamu-Asa more against BYU. It’s clear now that one reason he wasn’t in the game more was that his thumb was still bothering him. home.blurb: Miami returns to all-white stormtroopers for Halloween night trip to North Carolina Skip to main content About Hurricanes All-Time Football Lists Hurricanes All-Time Basketball Lists Miami Hurricanes Basketball Recruiting The Joe Gaither Show on CanesCentral The Miami Hurricanes will wear their all-white "Stormtrooper" combination for Saturday night's Halloween game against the North Carolina Tar Heels. Miami announced the look on Thursday, pairing white helmets with white jerseys and white pants (the program's standard road uniform). The No. 1 Hurricanes are undefeated in the combination this season after road wins at Stanford (45-6), Wake Forest (33-20) and Clemson (41-13). All white, all business 🙌 pic.twitter.com/dpVbfdILLx North Carolina enters at 4-3 overall and 2-2 in ACC play, while Miami (7-0, 5-0 ACC) arrives as a two-touchdown favorite. The Hurricanes are seeking their first win in Chapel Hill since 2017 and first victory in the series since 2018. North Carolina has won the past five meetings and holds a series edge 16-11. The Hurricanes have largely stuck to a simple rotation. The all-white Stormtroopers have served as the primary road look, and at home they have worn the traditional white helmet, orange jersey and white pants combination against Florida A&M and Florida State. The green alternate (white helmet, green jersey, green pants) appeared once, in a 52-3 win over Central Michigan. Last week against Pittsburgh, Miami debuted the home version of its 2001 Tribute throwbacks to honor the 25th anniversary of the 2001 national championship team. The road version of those throwbacks (white jersey with green pants) has not yet been used. Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB Happy Halloween, Ohio State fans . The Buckeyes (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) will try to maintain their No. 2 ranking Saturday night and attempt to knock off a desperate USC Trojans (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten) team still fighting for their CFP lives. With kickoff drawing closer, how does a Buckeyes team no longer led by quarterback Julian Sayin fare on the road? Scroll to find this week’s staff predictions, as I am all alone in first place at 7-0 so far this season. It’ll just be without Julian Sayin as its starting quarterback. Since Sayin went down, Ohio State on SI (and I included) have done our best to bring Buckeye Nation as many perspectives as possible as the season resumes Saturday night in Los Angeles against the USC Trojans. Given the parity in this year's wacky college football season, the Buckeyes have yet to have a true reality-check moment. This week isn’t it either. The Badgers, who play the Iowa Hawkeyes earlier in the day’s action, suffocated the Trojans in all areas last week in Madison in one of the sport’s most shocking upsets. Although Halloween night could call for a spooky outcome (pun purposely intended), it’s hard to pick against Ohio State in Big Ten play, regardless of who the quarterback ends up being, until it loses in league play. So far, I’m the lone undefeated picker this season, so riding the hot hand with coach Ryan Day’s team against a depleted Trojans bunch seems like a smart pick (although all-time series history says otherwise). Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 24, USC 14 Ohio State has reached the crux of its season, not necessarily because of where they stand in Big Ten competition at this point in its schedule, but because we don’t know for sure what the Buckeyes will look like without star quarterback Julian Sayin for the foreseeable future. Not to take anything away from the 6-2 Trojans, but what was originally supposed to be a road game against a solid-but-not-elite conference opponent has now shifted its focus entirely on how the Buckeyes will look with a freshman starting at quarterback, be it true freshman Luke Fahey or redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair. Having said that, Ohio State still wields a deeper and more talented roster overall, headlined by the best player in the game, wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. The Buckeyes’ staff has more than enough resources to work with to keep whichever quarterback ends up starting well protected scheme-wise. Look for a lot of quick passes and screens on offense, while the defense figures out a way to pressure Jayden Maiava into committing mistakes, just like Wisconsin did last week. With the Buckeyes being favored by a touchdown on the spread (-7), I’m picking them to cover thanks to another solid performance on defense. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 24, USC 21 The Wisconsin Badgers’ 24-7 win over USC last Saturday has Ohio State fans understandably wondering whether the Buckeyes will follow a comparable game plan. I am guessing that Luke Fahey will be the starting quarterback, and that the coaching staff has emphasized to Fahey to play efficiently in a style reminiscent of when Julian Sayin made his first start at home vs. Texas in 2025. The USC defensive line has the pass rushing ability to get after an opposing quarterback, and I believe Fahey will use his legs to get out of the pocket and make positive yards to keep drives alive. Ohio State's defense is going to be tested all game against a formidable USC offense, despite the issues that the Trojans had last week in Madison. Maybe it's wishful thinking on my part, but this game has some serious Tresselball vibes for me going into Saturday night against an USC team that has its back to the wall. Yards and points may be difficult for the Buckeyes to earn, but I believe the Buckeyes will exhale when Connor Hawkins makes a late field goal in the final minutes of the contest. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, USC 14 For the first time during Ryan Day’s tenure as Ohio State head coach, a backup quarterback will start for the Buckeyes in a Big Ten matchup. It is still unknown if that starter will be true freshman Luke Fahey, or former 5-star sophomore Tavien St. Clair. Although, what is known coming into this matchup is that the USC defense has been one of the worst defenses against the pass in the Big Ten this season. Learning curves should be there for whatever quarterback is penciled to start in Los Angeles against the Trojans, but Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith and the other pass-catchers in this room should still perform well and keep the Buckeye offense afloat. The run game will also be watched closely, as more will be expected from this group and it'll get a good test against a strong USC front. USC quarterback Jayden Maiava should make some plays to keep this game competitive, but expect the Ohio State front to stifle an inconsistent rushing attack from the Trojans and force some turnovers to swing the momentum in the Buckeyes’ favor, giving them their 6th straight win and first at USC since 1946.
