One of the more intriguing matchups on the Week 9 college football calendar finds the Buckeyes going on the road against the Trojans without Julian Sayin under center. How does that affect what happens in this battle of college football blue bloods? How Ohio State can win Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates a touchdown with with wide receiver Devin McCuin (3) during the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium Stadium in Bloomington, Ind. on Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Regardless of concerns at quarterback, Ohio State has the more complete statistical profile, particularly on defense. The Buckeyes are allowing just 13.4 points and 264.3 total yards per game, ranking fourth and sixth nationally, respectively. Their run defense has been especially effective, giving up only 92.9 rushing yards per game. It should have a decisive edge against a USC ground game that is 105th in FBS and totaling just 131 yards on average. Offensively, Jeremiah Smith has been spectacular yet again. The undefendable wide receiver and Heisman favorite has 984 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns on 52 catches. Even without Sayin, Ohio State can lean on its defense, establish Bo Jackson in the trenches, slow the game down, get the football into Smith's hands, and let him create after the catch. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Maybe relying on USC's defense to win a game hasn't always been a great idea. Applying enough pressure on the edges to rattle Sayin's replacement could give this talented offense enough breathing room to make this interesting. The Trojans are averaging 303.6 passing yards per game, ranking 10th nationally, with quarterback Jayden Maiava throwing for 2,303 yards and 19 touchdowns. USC also converts 50.5 percent of its third downs, the 14th-best rate in the country. That ability to sustain drives could be important against an Ohio State defense that has allowed opponents to convert just 38 percent of third downs. The Trojans need Maiava to protect the football and attack downfield over top OSU's front line defenders. Defensively, USC must pressure the inexperienced Buckeyes quarterback and prevent him from developing any early rhythm. More: Predicting Big Ten football scores for Week 9's biggest games Who wins, and why? Make no mistake: the absence of Julian Sayin distributing to the Buckeyes' talented wideouts is a real problem. USC, whatever its defensive lapses in the Riley era, has a legitimate opportunity to make this uncomfortable. Still, Ohio State has a significant defensive advantage overall, allowing just 13 points per game and has an important edge countering the Trojans' ground game that can reduce that offense to one dimension. USC will have opportunities, but Ohio State's defensive consistency ultimately proves to be the edge in the second half. The Big Lead prediction: Ohio State 30, USC 23

picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Baylor Bears vs. UCF Knights in Week 9 Without Dave Aranda Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL Bears In The Pros It's been a disastrous two weeks for the Baylor Bears. After dominating Arizona State and looking like the Bears could be a real threat, Baylor suffered back-to-back losses to TCU and Kansas, dropping the Bears to 4-3 on the season . The loss to Kansas also ended the Dave Aranda era in Waco. In his seventh season, Aranda was fired and Joe Klanderman will lead the Bears for the remainder of the season as the interim head coach . Klanderman looks to reignite the Baylor Bears and have a strong finish to the season. Baylor will look to get back into the win column on Friday night when the Bears take on UCF . Here's how the staff of Baylor on SI sees the game going. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Baylor's defense has been great this season and Klanderman has re-established the Bears' defense. But you have to wonder if there will be any setbacks from Dave Aranda not being on the sidelines any longer and Klanderman taking on the head coach role, while calling the defense. Baylor's defense has been great this season and Klanderman has re-established the Bears' defense. But you have to wonder if there will be any setbacks from Dave Aranda not being on the sidelines any longer and Klanderman taking on the head coach role, while calling the defense. UCF has a good offense and Keyone Jenkins has been legit . The Knights just beat BYU and a hangover is certainly possible, but it's not like Baylor has been playing great football. What worries me is the Bears' offensive line. DJ Lagway has been asked to do everything for this offense, and the offensive line can't block for the run game. If Baylor can't run the ball again, it's going to be tough sledding. I look for the home team to make one too many plays. Final score: UCF 27, Baylor 24 Baylor comes off a tough loss to Kansas and has a shorter week facing off against a UCF team that just beat the number 2 ranked team in the country. Should be mostly a passing game given the defenses in this matchup. Baylor has struggled to get the run game going and UCF has had one of the best run defenses in the country right now. Expect a high air-raid offense from both sides, and multiple touchdowns. Baylor will be in their first game without head coach Aranda after getting let go Sunday. My guess is that they will pull one together and slightly outscore this team coming off a big win. After the past two weeks saw Baylor lose to TCU and Kansas, fire Dave Aranda, name Joe Klanderman interim head coach, and have a shortened week of preparation for their Friday night contest against UCF, the Bears are up against the wall in terms of their season. They've officially hit the big red "panic" button on the season and fired Aranda in hopes of seemingly not losing the entire fan base. However, the competition still remains, and even with Aranda no longer with the team, the offense is still the same squad that has been struggling to produce since returning to play after the bye week. Baylor's defense is going to cause havoc for UCF's QB Keyone Jenkins and probably even record another 4+ SK 7+ TFL game. Potentially even forcing Jenkins into throwing an interception or two, the outcome of this game won't be the fault of the Bears' defense. There's only so much one side of the ball can do, after all. If the Bears O-line remains unable to successfully push back the opposing D-line, it's going to again lead to three-and-outs or otherwise quickly ended drives. Not to mention that an unsuccessful O-line will inevitably force DJ Lagway into uncomfortable throws and rushed decisions against UCF's team currently in the top 20 in the nation with a +5 turnover margin. Penalties have been a big problem for the Bears this season, especially last week, totaling a dozen for 116 yards. Averaging 74 yards a game in penalties is rough and only hurts the Bears overall. However, I don't expect that trend to end any time soon, maybe not for over 100 yards, but Baylor is going to give up a lot of yards that they didn't have to again this week. I would love nothing more than to watch the offense and defense come out and click on all cylinders, but this has been a not-so-normal week. Fully expecting the Bears to be competitive, I don't however expect them to be able to overcome their recent struggles offensively. Final score: UCF 20, Baylor 17 Blake Hollingsworth Hopefully I’m wrong, but I just don’t see Baylor coming out on top in interim head coach Joe Klanderman’s debut. UCF is unbeaten at home and coming off a double-overtime upset of previously undefeated No. 2 BYU. DJ Lagway should have a few chances to connect on deep passes against a UCF defense allowing nearly 240 passing yards per game. However, the Knights lead the Big 12 with 12 forced turnovers, including seven interceptions, which could be a problem for a Baylor offense averaging only 17.3 points in its four Power Four matchups outside its blowout win over Arizona State. Baylor’s defense will keep the game competitive per usual, but the Bears’ struggles with penalties, red-zone efficiency and offensive consistency are difficult to overlook. With UCF carrying momentum into Friday’s matchup, I’m picking the Knights to hand Baylor its third consecutive loss. picks.headline: Baylor Football Staff Picks: Over/Under Predictions For Week 9 vs. UCF
picks.blurb: Baylor Football Staff Picks: Over/Under Predictions For Week 9 vs. UCF Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL Bears In The Pros Week 9 is here and Baylor could look like a different team when it takes the field. The Bears are headed down to Orlando for a Friday night contest against the Knights . UCF is coming off an incredible overtime win over BYU, which gave the Cougars their first loss of the season. As for Baylor, the Bears fired Dave Aranda in his seventh season at the helm. Joe Klanderman has taken over as interim head coach and Baylor's coaching search is underway . Baylor on SI came up with some game props and picked what might happen on Friday night. DJ Lagway throws for O/U 239.5 passing yards IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop - OVER Trent Knoop - OVER DJ Lagway has been over this total in two of his last four games, but it does appear that Lagway is getting healthier, which only bodes well for the Bears' offense. UCF doesn't have a great passing defense, and with Baylor struggling to run the ball, Lagway will have to throw to win. Bennett Parker - OVER Personally, I would not touch Lagway O/U lines with a six-foot pole. Through seven games, I still don’t know what to think about his arm talent and decision making. It could very well be another 50% completion, ugly game for Lagway. However, if Baylor plays ‘free’ and ‘energized’ like they have been stressing, Lagway will be at his best and cruise past this line with the help of some trusty receivers and their yards after catch ability. Brad Teague - OVER There is absolutely no reason that DJ Lagway should be under 239 passing yards this week. Yes, Dave Aranda was just fired; but OC Jake Spavital has been calling the offensive plays this season, and is allegedly being now given "the freedom to be as creative as he wants to be" as interim head coach Joe Klanderman said during Media Availability on Monday. He only had 236 yards passing against Kansas last week, but I expect Lagway to excel this week against UCF, playing more freely, and finding numerous receivers on his way to having more than 240 yards passing. I'm taking the OVER on this one. Grant Peterson - OVER I’m leaning toward the over on this one. Even in games where Baylor has struggled offensively, Lagway has found a way to cover this line. I also think Jake Spavital will get creative and find ways to open up the passing game for this offense. Tyler Gillum - OVER UCF’s pass defense has been inconsistent this year averaging just about 240 passing yards per game this year. and Lagway hasn't been under 225 since the Colorado game, coming back from injury. Baylor's defense has O/U 2.5 sacks against UCF IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Trent Knoop - UNDER Trent Knoop - UNDER UCF is a top-five team in the Big 12 in sacks allowed. Baylor has an aggressive defense and should get to Keyone Jenkins. But Jenkins is a mobile quarterback who can escape pressure. Scott Frost will dial up some quick passes on Friday in hopes of not allowing Jenkins to stand in the pocket and take heat. The defensive line and linebacker play have been the cornerstone of the Bears’ defense and will continue to be against UCF. Klanderman has sent some well-timed blitzes, and knows how to keep the opposing QB off balance. The Bears had five sacks against Kansas and should at least scare that mark again on Friday. The Bears have the 2nd most sacks in all of the FBS in the first half of games with 17. Baylor has had 3 or more QB sacks in every game except against LA Tech back in September, I don't expect that trend to slow down any time soon. UCF QB Keyone Jenkins, as a playmaker, is going to look to take advantage of Baylor's aggression on the defensive line, but I fully expect Coach Klanderman and the Bears defense to be prepared for exactly that. This game has the potential for a high-count of TFLs, Sks, and FFs . I'm taking an emphatic OVER on this one. Grant Peterson - UNDER Baylor’s defense has been great at generating pressure all season, but I think they’ll finish with two sacks in this matchup. UCF has only allowed more than two sacks in one game this season. The Knights gave up two sacks to both TCU and Houston, along with one sack to BYU and Oklahoma State. Although I’m taking the under, I wouldn’t be surprised to see the Bears come away with three sacks. Tyler Gillum - UNDER Although I do think they can get some pressure on UCF. I think it'll be just about two or maybe even one. Keyone Jenkins showed the ability to escape the pocket and make plays. BYU was able to get just one sack all game with their defense. My prediction is Baylor will likely be the same UCF QB Keyone Jenkins has O/U 250.5 passing yards vs. Baylor Baylor has a good defense, but the Bears have allowed the opposing quarterback to throw for over 251 yards in three of their last four games. Keyone Jenkins has thrown for over 251 yards in his last three outings. The Knights are riding the hot hand and Jenkins' up-tempo style of play can cause some havoc. The Baylor defense has a way of giving up a decent amount of yards without surrendering too many points, allowing 340 per game while averaging just 16.1 points against. The secondary tends to allow some long drives early in the game and the occasional explosive play downfield. I expect UCF to take advantage as much as they can early on. Brad Teague - UNDER He's had some bigger games recently against the 'Pokes (265 yards) and BYU (293 yards), but on the season Keyone Jenkins is only averaging 157 passing yards a game. Not to mention that late in the BYU game, Jenkins would make a visit to the medical tent after being shaken up on a play. There's a chance that his overall drop-backs and longer-developing throws may be limited this week against a Bears defense who will be looking to continue their aggressive gameplay. Provided that Baylor's secondary can limit the penalties being called on them, they're among the top units in all of college football and always hungry for another INT. Keyone Jenkins does not throw for 250 yards in this game; I'm taking the UNDER on this one, Baylor has done a good job of limiting explosive passing plays this season, and I think that trend will continue against UCF. If the Bears can prevent Jenkins from connecting on big plays, I don’t see him surpassing 250 passing yards against this defense. If this game turns into a shootout, he could go over, but I don’t expect that to happen. Although I believe Jenkins will have another solid game, 250 is a lot against this relentless defense. I'm gonna say it'll be just under, but not by much, Jenkins hasn't been under 250 since September against TCU, but the Bears should bring enough pressure for Jenkins to just miss that mark Baylor rushes for O/U 160.5 yards against UCF Until Baylor proves it can run the ball, it's hard to put trust in the run game. It's not due to the running backs themselves. I do think Baylor has a good stable of backs, but the offensive line has been too inconsistent for my liking. This game will come down to DJ Lagway's arm. If Baylor intends on winning this game, they have no choice but to run the ball and run it well. Lagway has shown that he is back to 100% and the O-line is playing with a fire lit under them after struggling in the last couple of games. While I am not convinced by the Bears’ ground game whatsoever, they will get over this total with a lot of help from Lagway. There is zero reason why the Bears shouldn't be able to be well over this mark; except there are, in fact, five reasons why Baylor could miss this target. The Bears offensive line has not had great success this season at fully establishing a solid push and a dominant running game. They're working hard, like to block with and for each other and the Bears team, and seem to be giving it their all; but they've been ineffective throughout most of the season. They've had a 94.5% success rate of keeping the pocket clean on pass plays this season, but have only been able to gain 3.79 rushing yards a carry this season. Currently the Bears are averaging 146.14 rushing yards per game, and unless Dave Aranda getting fired is the catalyst these guys needed to become a stronger unit, I don't see Baylor gaining more than 160 rushing yards; I'm taking the UNDER. Baylor’s running game has been an issue all season, and I don’t expect that to change against the Knights. Against TCU, Baylor averaged just 1.6 yards per carry. Even against Kansas, one of the worst rushing defenses in the conference, the Bears averaged only 3.5 yards per carry, including Lagway’s rushing yards. Based on Baylor’s struggles on the ground this season, I’m taking the under on 160.5 rushing yards. After a rough two weeks of running the ball for Baylor, I don't expect much to change in this one. UCF is coming off a huge win and is ranked 38th in the country in rushing yards allowed on defense. It's going to be a real struggle if the Bears want to move the ball on the ground, and early passing will likely be needed to get any type of momentum on offense. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. home.blurb: The team built its offseason around the addition of Alonza Barnett III , a two-year starter at James Madison fresh off Sun Belt Conference Player of the Year honors and a trip to the College Football Playoff. Frost's staff protected its sizable financial investment in Barnett, holding him out of all 15 spring practice sessions as a precaution. Baylor 's vaunted defensive front knocked Jenkins out in the third quarter of Friday's 41-9 defeat. Frost said the senior reaggravated an ankle problem, though the severity is unknown. Barnett returned from a five-game absence but could not provide the spark needed to ignite a comeback. UCF flip-flopped through four quarterbacks in 2025, Frost's return to Orlando after seven years — five as Nebraska's head coach. ORLANDO — It's another round of musical chairs at quarterback for the UCF Knights , a situation Scott Frost hoped to avoid when the transfer portal opened in 2026. Plans changed two games into the campaign when Barnett sustained a "fairly significant" hamstring injury , sidelining him for more than a month. Keyone Jenkins , a 33-game starter at Florida International, stepped in and steadied the ship at the start of Big 12 play. He led the Knights to their highest-ranked win in program history Oct. 24, a 39-31 double-overtime classic against BYU , with 293 passing yards and four total touchdowns. However, seats could switch again for the stretch run after yet another injury. As November approaches, and with UCF needing another pair of wins to achieve bowl eligibility, uncertainty exists about the starting signal-caller going forward. "I've said a lot that I feel good about our quarterbacks, whoever's in there," Frost said. A familiar problem for UCF head coach Scott Frost Cam Fancher lasted less than a half before getting clobbered on a sack, injuring his back, and then sustained broken ribs at Cincinnati a month later. Tayven Jackson started 10 times, but battled several ailments, including a shoulder joint sprain at Kansas State. Jacurri Brown injured his shoulder in that same game and did not see the field the rest of the year. Fourth-stringer Davi Belfort, now a wide receiver at James Madison, made a few appearances, throwing a game-sealing interception in a loss to Houston. Thus, the root problem lies in the support system, as opposed to strictly a QB's individual performance or toughness. "Whoever was playing quarterback, it's going to be hard if we don't block better and create a running game," Frost said. "I mean, we couldn't get anything going in the first half. We couldn't get a run game going, and we didn't protect very well."
